units.zh: 序
units.en: Preface
units.literal: Preface

units.zh: 漢宣帝有言：「百姓所以安其田里而無歎息愁恨之心者，政平訟理也。
units.en: Emperor Xuan of Han had a saying: 'The reason the common people can rest secure in their fields and lanes without sighing in resentment is that government is evenhanded and lawsuits are fairly judged.
units.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han had a saying: 'The reason the common people can rest secure in their fields and lanes without sighing in resentment is that government is evenhanded and lawsuits are fairly judged.

units.zh: 與我共此者，其唯良二千石乎！」
units.en: Those who share this with me—are they not only the good commandery governors [at two thousand shi]?'
units.literal: Those who share this with me—are they not only the good commandery governors [at two thousand shi]?'

units.zh: 此則長吏之官，實為撫導之本。
units.en: In other words, the county-level chief is the foundation of good rule and sound guidance.
units.literal: This shows that the office of senior magistrate is truly the root of comforting and guiding the people.

units.zh: 是以東裏相鄭，西門宰鄴，潁川黃霸，蜀郡文翁，或吏不敢欺，或人懷其惠，或教移齊魯，或政務寬和，斯並惇史播其徽音，良能以為准的。
units.en: From Zi Chan in Zheng and Ximen Bao in Ye to Huang Ba in Yingchuan and Wen Weng in Shu—some overawed corrupt clerks, some won deep affection, some made instruction equal that of Qi and Lu, some ruled with calm kindness—history praised them, and capable officials ever since have taken them as their yardstick.
units.literal: Therefore Dongli Zichan as minister of Zheng, Ximen Bao as magistrate of Ye, Huang Ba of Yingchuan, Wen Weng of Shu commandery—some caused clerks not to dare deceive them, some caused the people to cherish their kindness, some carried instruction into Qi and Lu, some administered affairs with lenience and harmony; these were all proclaimed by earnest historians and taken as standards by able men.

units.zh: 有晉肇茲王業，光啟霸圖，授方任能，經文緯武。
units.en: The Jin house raised its kingship and unfurled ambition across the realm, putting the right men in the right posts and pairing civil order with military strength.
units.literal: When Jin founded its royal enterprise here and opened wide its hegemonic design, it assigned regions and employed worthies, ordering the civil realm and arraying the martial.

units.zh: 泰始受禪，改物君臨，纂三葉之鴻基，膺百王之大寶，勞心庶績，垂意黎元，申敕守宰之司，婁發憂矜之詔，辭旨懇切，誨諭殷勤，欲使直道正身，抑末敦本。
units.en: From the Taishi accession onward the throne changed hands peacefully; the dynasty inherited three generations of accumulated power and the nominal legitimacy of a long line of kings, toiled at every branch of administration, looked after the commoners, lectured prefects and magistrates again and again, and issued repeated edicts of heartfelt concern—demanding integrity, discipline, and a return to fundamental virtues.
units.literal: At Taishi, receiving the abdication and changing the mandate to rule as sovereign, inheriting the vast foundation of three reigns and receiving the great treasure passed down through a hundred kings, laboring over the myriad tasks of government and turning attention to the common people, repeatedly charging those who guarded and governed districts and issuing again and again edicts of anxious sympathy—wording earnest and urgent, instruction diligent—wishing to make officials walk the straight path and correct themselves, restraining the secondary and strengthening the root.

units.zh: 當此時也，可謂農安其業，吏盡其能者歟！
units.en: At that moment it seemed farmers could stay at their plows and officials actually did their jobs.
units.literal: In such an hour, could one not say that farmers were secure in their occupations and clerks fulfilled their duties?

units.zh: 而帝寬厚足以君人，明威未能厲俗，政刑以之私謁，賄賂於此公行，結綬者以放濁為通，彈冠者以苟得為貴，流遁忘反，浸以為常。
units.en: But imperial lenience let him govern without inspiring awe; customs did not stiffen. Justice bent to pull and patronage; gifts passed hands in broad daylight. Men who wore official cords treated laxity and graft as sophistication; men who entered office prized whatever they could grab. People slid away and forgot to return until vice passed for routine.
units.literal: Yet the emperor's generous tolerance sufficed to rule men as lord, but his awesome clarity could not steel custom; government and punishments were bent by private soliciting, bribes ran openly here; those who tied their seals took looseness and corruption as 'getting through,' those who brushed caps took grasping gain as honor; drift and escape became forgetfulness of return, gradually entrenched as normal.

units.zh: 劉毅抗賣官之言，當時以為矯枉，察其風俗，豈虛也哉！
units.en: When Liu Yi denounced the sale of offices, contemporaries called his remedy overwrought—yet look at how morals actually behaved, and his warning rings true.
units.literal: Liu Yi spoke out against selling offices—people of the time thought him excessive in correcting a fault; observe the customs—was it empty talk?

units.zh: 爰及惠懷，中州鼎沸，逮于江左，晉政多門，元帝比少康之隆，處仲為梗，海西微昌邑之罪，元子亂常，既權逼是憂，故羈縻成俗。
units.en: Under Hui and Huai the heartland exploded into chaos; after the court crossed to the south, authority fractured among factions. Emperor Yuan likened his restoration to Shao Kang's revival, yet Wang Dun blocked him; the Prince of Haixi reproduced King Changyi's offenses on a lesser scale, and Huan Wen upset the proper order. Once coercion by the powerful became the worry, loose restraint hardened into custom.
units.literal: Reaching Emperor Hui and Emperor Huai, the Central Plain boiled like a cauldron; down to the left bank of the Yangzi, Jin policy had many doors. The Yuan Emperor compared himself to the prosperity of Shao Kang, but Wang Dun was an obstruction; the Prince of Haixi raised King Changyi of Han's faults on a small scale, and Huan Wen disturbed the norm; once power and coercion became the worry, lax restraint hardened into custom.

units.zh: 蒞職者為身擇利，銓綜者為人擇官，下僚多英俊之才，勢位必高門之胄，遂使良能之績僅有存焉。
units.en: Officeholders picked rewards for themselves; personnel clerks picked jobs for friends. Staff might be brilliant, yet real power stayed with great-clan heirs, so genuine administrative talent surfaced only here and there.
units.literal: Those who took office chose profit for themselves; those who handled appointments chose posts for others; subordinates were often men of outstanding talent, but powerful positions inevitably went to sons of eminent houses—so that the achievements of the truly able survived only in scattered instances.

units.zh: 雖復茂弘以明允贊經綸，安石以時宗鎮雅俗，然外虞孔熾，內難方殷，而匡救彌縫，方免傾覆，弘風革弊，彼則未遑。
units.en: Wang Dao lent steady judgment to statecraft and Xie An anchored elite opinion, but foreign crises flared and domestic strife seethed; they spent every ounce of energy merely preventing collapse, with no room left to reform manners root and branch.
units.literal: Although again Wang Dao with enlightened fairness assisted in ordering the realm, and Xie An as pillar of the age steadied refined custom, still outer alarms blazed fiercely and inner troubles ran deep; patching and mending barely averted collapse—there was no leisure to spread transforming influence and reform abuses.

units.zh: 今采其政績可稱者，以為《良吏傳》。
units.en: This chapter gathers officials whose deeds on the job merit remembrance—the Good Officials.
units.literal: Now I select those whose administrative records deserve praise and make of them the 'Biographies of Good Officials.'

units.zh: 魯芝
units.en: Lu Zhi
units.literal: Lu Zhi

units.zh: 魯芝，字世英，扶風郿人也。
units.en: Lu Zhi (courtesy Shiying) came from Mei county in Fufeng.
units.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Shiying, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.

units.zh: 世有名德，為西州豪族。
units.en: His clan had long been celebrated for integrity and ranked among the great houses of the northwest.
units.literal: For generations his family had enjoyed renowned virtue and was a powerful clan of the western provinces.

units.zh: 父為郭氾所害，芝繈褓流離，年十七，乃移居雍，耽思墳籍。
units.en: Guo Si murdered his father; Zhi was still an infant when the family was scattered. At seventeen he settled in Yong and buried himself in the canon.
units.literal: His father was killed by Guo Si; Zhi, still in swaddling clothes, wandered destitute, and at seventeen he moved to Yong, immersing himself in study of the classics.

units.zh: 郡舉上計吏，州辟別駕。
units.en: The commandery nominated him accounts clerk; the province called him up as provincial aide.
units.literal: The commandery recommended him as clerk for the annual accounting; the province summoned him as provincial aide.

units.zh: 魏車騎將軍郭淮為雍州刺史，深敬重之。
units.en: Wei general Guo Huai, as inspector of Yong, treated him with exceptional respect.
units.literal: Guo Huai, General of Chariots and Cavalry of Wei, was Inspector of Yong Province and held him in deep respect.

units.zh: 舉孝廉，除郎中。
units.en: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he received a gentleman-of-the-interior appointment.
units.literal: He was recommended as filial and incorrupt and appointed gentleman of the interior.

units.zh: 會蜀相諸葛亮侵隴右，淮復請芝為別駕。
units.en: When Zhuge Liang of Shu struck Longyou, Guo Huai again kept him on as provincial aide.
units.literal: When the Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang invaded Longyou, Huai again asked Zhi to serve as provincial aide.

units.zh: 事平，薦於公府，辟大司馬曹真掾，轉臨淄侯文學。
units.en: After hostilities ended he went to the central ministries, served as staff to Grand Marshal Cao Zhen, then moved to tutor of literature for the marquis of Linzi.
units.literal: When the affair was settled, [Zhi] was recommended to the ministerial offices and summoned as aide to the Grand Marshal Cao Zhen; he was transferred to literary instructor to the Marquis of Linzi.

units.zh: 鄭袤薦于司空王朗，朗即加禮命。
units.en: Zheng Mao introduced him to Wang Lang, minister of works, who honored him with an immediate posting.
units.literal: Zheng Mao recommended him to Minister of Works Wang Lang, and Lang at once treated him with courtesy and appointed him.

units.zh: 後拜騎都尉、參軍事、行安南太守，遷尚書郎。
units.en: He rose through Commandant of Cavalry, military adviser, acting administrator of An'nan, and gentleman at the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: Later he was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, joined military affairs, acted as Administrator of An'nan, was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 曹真出督關右，又參大司馬軍事。
units.en: When Cao Zhen supervised the region west of the passes, Zhi again served on the grand marshal's staff.
units.literal: When Cao Zhen went out to supervise the west of the Pass, [Zhi] again joined the Grand Marshal's military staff.

units.zh: 真薨，宣帝代焉，乃引芝參驃騎軍事，轉天水太守。
units.en: After Cao Zhen died Sima Yi took his place and attached Zhi to the agile-cavalry command; Zhi then became administrator of Tianshui.
units.literal: When Zhen died, the Emperor Xuan [Sima Yi] replaced him and then brought Zhi in to join the military staff of the General of Agile Cavalry; [Zhi] was transferred to Administrator of Tianshui.

units.zh: 郡鄰於蜀，數被侵掠，戶口減削，寇盜充斥，芝傾心鎮衛，更造城市，數年間舊境悉復。
units.en: Tianshui lay against Shu and suffered repeated raids: population fell and bandits multiplied. Zhi threw himself into defense, rebuilt the city, and within a few years the district recovered its old bounds.
units.literal: The commandery bordered Shu and repeatedly suffered invasion and plunder; households dwindled and bandits swarmed. Zhi devoted himself to guarding and defending, rebuilt the walls and town, and within a few years the former territory was fully restored.

units.zh: 遷廣平太守。
units.en: He was transferred to Guangping.
units.literal: He was promoted to Administrator of Guangping.

units.zh: 天水夷夏慕德，老幼赴闕獻書，乞留芝。
units.en: Yi tribesmen and Han alike cherished him; young and old traveled to the capital with petitions begging the court to keep him.
units.literal: Both Yi and Han Chinese in Tianshui admired his virtue; old and young went to the capital to submit petitions asking that Zhi be kept [in office].

units.zh: 魏明帝許焉，仍策書嘉歎，勉以黃霸之美，加討寇將軍。
units.en: Emperor Ming agreed, issued a warm commendation comparing him to Huang Ba, and added the title General Who Suppresses Brigands.
units.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei granted this; an edict was still issued praising him, encouraging him with the fine example of Huang Ba, and he was additionally granted the title General Who Suppresses Brigands.

units.zh: 曹爽輔政，引為司馬。
units.en: When Cao Shuang controlled the regency he took Zhi on as marshal.
units.literal: When Cao Shuang dominated the government, [Shuang] brought [Zhi] in as marshal.

units.zh: 芝屢有讜言嘉謀，爽弗能納。
units.en: Zhi gave blunt, sound advice again and again; Shuang refused to listen.
units.literal: Zhi repeatedly offered forthright counsel and fine plans, which Shuang could not accept.

units.zh: 及宣帝起兵誅爽，芝率餘眾犯門斬關，馳出赴爽，勸爽曰：「公居伊周之位，一旦以罪見黜，雖欲牽黃犬，復可得乎！
units.en: When the Emperor Xuan [Sima Yi] raised troops to execute Shuang, Zhi led the remaining troops to force the gates and break through the barriers, galloping out to join Shuang, and urged Shuang: 'You occupy the position of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—once you are dismissed for crime, even if you wished to lead a yellow dog [on a hunt], could you have it again?
units.literal: When the Emperor Xuan [Sima Yi] raised troops to execute Shuang, Zhi led the remaining troops to force the gates and break through the barriers, galloping out to join Shuang, and urged Shuang: 'You occupy the position of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—once you are dismissed for crime, even if you wished to lead a yellow dog [on a hunt], could you have it again?

units.zh: 若挾天子保許昌，杖大威以羽檄征四方兵，孰敢不從！
units.en: If you seize the Son of Heaven and hold Xuchang, wielding great awe and dispatching feathered summons to levy troops from the four quarters, who would dare not follow?
units.literal: If you seize the Son of Heaven and hold Xuchang, wielding great awe and dispatching feathered summons to levy troops from the four quarters, who would dare not follow?

units.zh: 舍此而去，欲就東市，豈不痛哉！」
units.en: To abandon this and depart, only to go to the eastern market [for execution]—how could it not be bitter?'
units.literal: To abandon this and depart, only to go to the eastern market [for execution]—how could it not be bitter?'

units.zh: 爽懦惑不能用，遂委身受戮。
units.en: Shuang was timid and bewildered and ignored him; he surrendered and died under the blade.
units.literal: Shuang was cowardly and confused and could not use [the advice]; he thereupon submitted his person and was executed.

units.zh: 芝坐爽下獄，當死，而口不訟直，志不苟免。
units.en: Zhi, tied to Shuang's faction, went to prison facing death, yet he neither whined for mercy nor grasped at an unworthy reprieve.
units.literal: Zhi, implicated under Shuang, was imprisoned and sentenced to death, yet he did not argue his innocence aloud and was resolved not to seek escape unworthily.

units.zh: 宣帝嘉之，赦而不誅。
units.en: Sima Yi admired him and spared his life.
units.literal: The Emperor Xuan admired him and pardoned him without execution.

units.zh: 俄而起為使持節、領護匈奴中郎將、振威將軍、并州刺史。
units.en: Soon he held credentials as commissioner, concurrent colonel of the central Xiongnu corps, General Who Rouses Might, and inspector of Bing.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed commissioner with credentials, concurrent Colonel for the Xiongnu of the Center, General Who Rouses Might, and Inspector of Bing Province.

units.zh: 以綏緝有方，遷大鴻臚。
units.en: His skill at pacifying and administering won him promotion to grand herald.
units.literal: For skilled pacification and administration he was promoted to Grand Herald.

units.zh: 高貴鄉公即位，賜爵關內侯，邑二百戶。
units.en: When the duke of Gaoguixiang became emperor, Zhi received a secondary marquisate inside the passes with two hundred households.
units.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang ascended the throne, [Zhi] was granted noble rank as secondary marquis within the passes, with an estate of two hundred households.

units.zh: 毌丘儉平，隨例增邑二百戶，拜揚武將軍、荆州刺史。
units.en: After Guanqiu Jian's rebellion was crushed his fief rose by another two hundred households by rule; he became General Who Displays Might and inspector of Jing.
units.literal: After Guanqiu Jian was pacified, by precedent his fief was increased by two hundred households; he was appointed General Who Displays Might and Inspector of Jing Province.

units.zh: 諸葛誕以壽春叛，文帝奉魏帝出征，徵兵四方，芝率荊州文武以為先驅。
units.en: When Zhuge Dan rose at Shou-chun, Sima Zhao marched with the Wei emperor and called troops from every quarter; Zhi led Jing's civil and military officers in the van.
units.literal: When Zhuge Dan rebelled at Shou-chun, Emperor Wen [Sima Zhao] led the Wei emperor on campaign, levying troops from the four quarters; Zhi led the civil and military officers of Jing Province as the vanguard.

units.zh: 誕平，進爵武進亭侯，又增邑九百戶。
units.en: After Dan fell he advanced to marquis of Wujin precinct with nine hundred more households.
units.literal: When Dan was pacified, his noble rank was advanced to Marquis of Wujin precinct, and another nine hundred households were added to his fief.

units.zh: 遷大尚書，掌刑理。
units.en: He entered the Masters of Writing with broadened duties and oversaw penal justice.
units.literal: He was promoted to Masters of Writing with expanded duties, in charge of penal administration.

units.zh: 常道鄉公即位，進爵斄城鄉侯，又增邑八百戶，遷監青州諸軍事、振武將軍、青州刺史，轉平東將軍。
units.en: When the duke of Changdao succeeded, his title rose to marquis of Lai township with eight hundred more households; he supervised Qing military affairs as General Who Displays Martial Might and inspector of Qing, then shifted to General Who Pacifies the East.
units.literal: When the Duke of Changdao Township ascended the throne, his noble rank was advanced to Marquis of Lai Township, another eight hundred households were added to his fief, he was promoted to supervise military affairs in Qing Province with concurrent appointment as General Who Displays Martial Might and Inspector of Qing Province, and transferred to General Who Pacifies the East.

units.zh: 五等建，封陰平伯。
units.en: Under the new five-rank nobility he became baron of Yinping.
units.literal: When the five ranks were established, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yinping.

units.zh: 武帝踐阼，轉鎮東將軍，進爵為侯。
units.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne Zhi became General Who Guards the East and full marquis.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, [Zhi] was transferred to General Who Guards the East and his noble rank was advanced to marquis.

units.zh: 帝以芝清忠履正，素無居宅，使軍兵為作屋五十間。
units.en: Seeing that Zhi was pure, loyal, and upright in conduct and had never owned a house, the emperor ordered fifty rooms built for him.
units.literal: Because Zhi was pure, loyal, and upright in conduct and had never owned a dwelling, the emperor had soldiers build fifty rooms for him.

units.zh: 芝以年及懸車，告老遜位，章表十餘上，於是徵為光祿大夫，位特進，給吏卒，門施行馬。
units.en: Feeling he had reached retiring age, he repeatedly memorialized to step down—more than ten times—until the court recalled him as minister of the imperial household at nominal salary with specially advanced rank, staff and guards, and the privilege of a barrier gate.
units.literal: Zhi, feeling his years had reached the age to hang up his carriage [retire], requested retirement and yielded his position; memorials ran to more than ten submissions—whereupon he was summoned as Minister of the Imperial Household with nominal salary only, rank specially advanced, given clerks and soldiers, and a barrier gate was erected at his door.

units.zh: 羊祜為車騎將軍，乃以位讓芝，曰：「光祿大夫魯芝潔身寡欲，和而不同，服事華髮，以禮終始，未蒙此選，臣更越之，何以塞天下之望！」
units.en: Yang Hu was General of Chariots and Cavalry and wished to yield his position to Zhi, saying: 'Minister of the Imperial Household Lu Zhi keeps himself pure with few desires, harmonizes without agreeing blindly, has served until his hair is hoary and observes ritual from first to last—he has not yet received this selection; if I leap past him, how shall I answer the hopes of the realm?'
units.literal: Yang Hu was General of Chariots and Cavalry and wished to yield his position to Zhi, saying: 'Minister of the Imperial Household Lu Zhi keeps himself pure with few desires, harmonizes without agreeing blindly, has served until his hair is hoary and observes ritual from first to last—he has not yet received this selection; if I leap past him, how shall I answer the hopes of the realm?'

units.zh: 上不從。
units.en: The emperor refused.
units.literal: The emperor did not consent.

units.zh: 其為人所重如是。
units.en: That was how highly peers valued him.
units.literal: Such was the esteem in which others held him.

units.zh: 泰始九年卒，年八十四。
units.en: In the ninth year of Taishi, he died at eighty-four.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi, he died at age eighty-four.

units.zh: 帝為舉哀，賵贈有加，諡曰貞，賜塋田百畝。
units.en: The emperor held mourning for him, burial gifts were given beyond the norm, his posthumous name was Zhen ('steadfast'), and he was granted a burial plot of one hundred mu.
units.literal: The emperor held mourning for him; burial gifts were augmented beyond the norm; his posthumous name was Zhen [Steadfast], and he was granted a burial plot of one hundred mu.

units.zh: 胡威
units.en: Hu Wei
units.literal: Hu Wei

units.zh: 胡威，字伯武，一名貔。
units.en: Hu Wei (courtesy Bowu), also known as Pi.
units.literal: Hu Wei, courtesy name Bowu, also called Pi.

units.zh: 淮南壽春人也。
units.en: He came from Shou-chun in Huainan.
units.literal: He was a native of Shou-chun in Huainan.

units.zh: 父質，以忠清著稱，少與鄉人蔣濟、硃績俱知名于江淮間，仕魏至征東將軍、荊州刺史。
units.en: His father Hu Zhi won fame for loyalty and rectitude; as a young man he stood alongside Jiang Ji and Zhu Ji from the same district across the Jiang-Huai region, rising in Wei to general who conquers the east and inspector of Jing.
units.literal: His father Zhi was famed for loyalty and purity; in youth he was known together with fellow villagers Jiang Ji and Zhu Ji throughout the lands between the Jiang and Huai, and served Wei up to General Who Conquers the East and Inspector of Jing Province.

units.zh: 威早厲志尚。
units.en: Wei shaped his ambitions early.
units.literal: Wei from his youth cultivated aspiration.

units.zh: 質之為荊州也，威自京都定省，家貧，無車馬僮僕，自驅驢單行。
units.en: When Hu Zhi governed Jing, Wei traveled from the capital to visit; the household was destitute—no cart, horses, or servants—so he rode a donkey by himself.
units.literal: When Zhi was Inspector of Jing Province, Wei came from the capital to visit his parents; the family was poor and had no carriage, horses, or servants—he drove a donkey alone.

units.zh: 每至客舍，躬放驢，取樵炊爨，食畢，復隨侶進道。
units.en: At every hostel he personally tended the donkey, gathered firewood, cooked his meal, ate, and moved on with other travelers.
units.literal: Whenever he reached an inn, he personally tended the donkey, gathered firewood to cook and boil [his food], and after eating continued on the road with fellow travelers.

units.zh: 既至，見父，停廄中十餘日。
units.en: On reaching his father he lodged in the stable over ten days.
units.literal: When he arrived he saw his father and stayed in the stable more than ten days.

units.zh: 告歸，父賜絹一匹為裝。
units.en: When he prepared to leave, his father gave him one bolt of silk for the road.
units.literal: When he announced his departure, his father gave him one bolt of silk for travel expenses.

units.zh: 威曰：「大人清高，不審于何得此絹？」
units.en: Wei said: 'Father, you are pure and lofty—from where did this silk come?'
units.literal: Wei said: 'Father, you are pure and lofty—from where did this silk come?'

units.zh: 質曰：「是吾俸祿之餘，以為汝糧耳。」
units.en: Zhi said: 'It is what remains of my salary, meant as provisions for you.'
units.literal: Zhi said: 'It is what remains of my salary, meant as provisions for you.'

units.zh: 威受之，辭歸。
units.en: Wei took it and set out for home.
units.literal: Wei accepted it and took leave to return.

units.zh: 質帳下都督先威未發，請假還家，陰資裝于百餘里，要威為伴，每事佐助。
units.en: Before Wei departed, his father's camp commandant took leave, rode ahead more than a hundred li, stocked supplies in secret, intercepted Wei as a traveling companion, and waited on him at every step.
units.literal: Before Wei had set out, the commander (dudu) under Zhi's tent asked leave and returned home, secretly supplied provisions over a hundred li down the road, intercepted Wei as a companion, and assisted him at every turn.

units.zh: 行數百里，威疑而誘問之，既知，乃取所賜絹與都督，謝而遣之。
units.en: After several hundred li Wei suspected something, drew the truth out, returned his father's silk to the commandant with thanks, and dismissed him.
units.literal: After several hundred li Wei grew suspicious and questioned him under pretense; once he knew [the truth], he took the silk his father had given him and gave it to the commandant, thanked him, and sent him away.

units.zh: 後因他信以白質，質杖都督一百，除吏名。
units.en: He then wrote his father; Hu Zhi had the commandant thrashed one hundred strokes and erased him from the roster.
units.literal: Later, through another messenger, he informed Zhi; Zhi had the commandant flogged one hundred strokes and struck his name from the rolls.

units.zh: 其父子清慎如此。
units.en: Such was their mutual purity and care.
units.literal: Thus father and son were pure and cautious to this degree.

units.zh: 於是名譽著聞。
units.en: His name soon traveled widely.
units.literal: Thereupon his reputation spread far.

units.zh: 拜侍御史，曆南鄉侯、安豐太守，遷徐州刺史。
units.en: He became attendant censor, marquis of Nanxiang, administrator of Anfeng, then inspector of Xu.
units.literal: He was appointed Attendant Censor, served as Marquis of Nanxiang, Administrator of Anfeng, and was promoted Inspector of Xu Province.

units.zh: 勤於政術，風化大行。
units.en: He worked his administrative craft tirelessly and reshaped local custom.
units.literal: He was diligent in governing technique; transforming influence spread broadly.

units.zh: 後入朝，武帝語及平生，因歎其父清，謂威曰：「卿孰與父清？」
units.en: Later he entered court; when Emperor Wu spoke of [his] whole life, he sighed at his father's purity and said to Wei: 'Between you and your father, who is the purer?'
units.literal: Later he entered court; when Emperor Wu spoke of [his] whole life, he sighed at his father's purity and said to Wei: 'Between you and your father, who is the purer?'

units.zh: 對曰：「臣不如也。」
units.en: He replied: 'Your servant is not the equal [of his father].'
units.literal: He replied: 'Your servant is not the equal [of his father].'

units.zh: 帝曰：「卿父以何勝耶？」
units.en: The emperor said: 'In what does your father surpass you?'
units.literal: The emperor said: 'In what does your father surpass you?'

units.zh: 對曰：「臣父清恐人知，臣清恐人不知，是臣不及遠也。」
units.en: He replied: 'My father's purity feared that others would know; your servant's purity fears that others would not know—there your servant falls far short.'
units.literal: He replied: 'My father's purity feared that others would know; your servant's purity fears that others would not know—there your servant falls far short.'

units.zh: 帝以威言直而婉，謙而順。
units.en: The emperor found the reply frank yet diplomatic, humble yet loyal.
units.literal: The emperor considered Wei's words straightforward yet tactful, modest yet compliant.

units.zh: 累遷監豫州諸軍事、右將軍、豫州刺史，入為尚書，加奉車都尉。
units.en: He rose to supervise Yu military affairs as General of the Right and inspector of Yu, entered the Masters of Writing, and received the additional title Commandant of Imperial Equipages.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to supervise military affairs in Yu Province with concurrent appointment as General of the Right and Inspector of Yu Province, entered [court] as Masters of Writing, and was additionally given Commandant of Imperial Equipages.

units.zh: 威嘗諫時政之寬，帝曰：「尚書郎以下，吾無所假借。」
units.en: Wei once remonstrated that current policy was too lenient; the emperor said: 'Below the gentlemen of the Masters of Writing, I grant no indulgence.'
units.literal: Wei once remonstrated that current policy was too lenient; the emperor said: 'Below the Masters of Writing supervisors, I grant no indulgence.'

units.zh: 威曰：「臣之所陳，豈在丞郎令史，正謂如臣等輩，始可以肅化明法耳。」
units.en: Wei said: 'What your servant has stated—how could it concern only assistants and clerks? It is precisely men of your servant's rank who must then be able to stiffen transformation and clarify the law.'
units.literal: Wei said: 'What your servant has stated—how could it concern only assistants and clerks? It is precisely men of your servant's rank who must then be able to stiffen transformation and clarify the law.'

units.zh: 拜前將軍、監青州諸軍事、青州刺史，以功封平春侯，
units.en: He took General of the Front, supervised Qing, served as Qing inspector, and earned the marquisate of Pingchun for merit.
units.literal: He was appointed General of the Front, supervised military affairs in Qing Province, and became Inspector of Qing Province; for merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingchun.

units.zh: 太康元年，卒於位，追贈使持節、都督青州諸軍事、鎮東將軍，余如故，諡曰烈。
units.en: In the first year of Taikang, he died in office. Posthumously he received credentials as commissioner and concurrent governor of Qing military affairs as General Who Guards the East, kept his other honors, and took the posthumous name Lie ('ardent').
units.literal: In the first year of Taikang, he died in office. Posthumously he was granted credentials as envoy and concurrently governor of military affairs in Qing Province, General Who Guards the East; his other titles remained as before. His posthumous name was Lie [Ardent].

units.zh: 子奕嗣。
units.en: His son Yi succeeded to the title.
units.literal: His son Yi inherited.

units.zh: 威子 奕
units.en: Hu Yi (son of Hu Wei)
units.literal: Hu Wei's son Yi

units.zh: 奕字次孫，仕至平東將軍。
units.en: Hu Yi (courtesy Cisun) reached General Who Pacifies the East.
units.literal: Yi, courtesy name Cisun, rose to General Who Pacifies the East.

units.zh: 威弟羆，字季象，亦有幹用，仕至益州刺史、安東將軍。
units.en: Hu Wei's younger brother Pi (courtesy Jixiang) was likewise capable, rising to inspector of Yi and General Who Calms the East.
units.literal: Wei's younger brother Pi, courtesy name Jixiang, was also capable and effective in office; he rose to Inspector of Yi Province and General Who Pacifies the East.

units.zh: 杜軫
units.en: Du Zhen
units.literal: Du Zhen

units.zh: 杜軫，字超宗，蜀郡成都人也。
units.en: Du Zhen (courtesy Chaozong) came from Chengdu in Shu.
units.literal: Du Zhen, courtesy name Chaozong, was a native of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

units.zh: 父雄，綿竹令。
units.en: His father Du Xiong had been magistrate of Mianzhu.
units.literal: His father Xiong was magistrate of Mianzhu.

units.zh: 軫師事譙周，博涉經書。
units.en: Du Zhen studied under Qiao Zhou and widely explored the classics.
units.literal: Zhen studied under Qiao Zhou and broadly read the classics.

units.zh: 州辟不就，為郡功曹史。
units.en: The provincial summons he declined; he worked as the commandery clerk of merit.
units.literal: The province summoned him but he did not go; he served as clerk of merit for the commandery.

units.zh: 時鄧艾至成都，軫白太守曰：「今大軍來征，必除舊佈新，明府宜避之，此全福之道也。」
units.en: When Deng Ai arrived at Chengdu, Zhen reported to the Administrator: 'Now the great army has come on campaign—it will surely remove the old and spread the new; you, sir, should withdraw from [office]; that is the way to preserve good fortune.'
units.literal: When Deng Ai arrived at Chengdu, Zhen reported to the Administrator: 'Now the great army has come on campaign—it will surely remove the old and spread the new; you, sir, should withdraw from [office]; that is the way to preserve good fortune.'

units.zh: 太守乃出。
units.en: The administrator resigned at once.
units.literal: The Administrator thereupon went out [left office].

units.zh: 艾果遣其參軍牽弘自之郡，弘問軫前守所在，軫正色對曰：「前守達去就之機，輒自出官舍以俟君子。」
units.en: Ai indeed sent his adjutant Qian Hong to proceed to the commandery himself; Hong asked Zhen where the former Administrator was, and Zhen answered with stern demeanor: "The former Administrator grasped the moment to advance or withdraw and left the official residence on his own to await a gentleman."
units.literal: Ai indeed sent his adjutant Qian Hong to proceed to the commandery himself; Hong asked Zhen where the former Administrator was, and Zhen answered with stern demeanor: "The former Administrator grasped the moment to advance or withdraw and left the official residence on his own to await a gentleman."

units.zh: 弘器之，命復為功曹，軫固辭。
units.en: Qian Hong thought highly of him and tried to put him back in the clerk-of-merit post; Du Zhen refused outright.
units.literal: Hong esteemed him and ordered him restored as clerk of merit; Zhen firmly declined.

units.zh: 察孝廉，除建寧令，導以德政，風化大行，夷夏悅服。
units.en: Raised as filial and incorrupt, he governed Jianning with benevolent rule until custom changed across the district and every community, tribal or Chinese, accepted his authority.
units.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he was appointed magistrate of Jianning; guided by virtuous government, transforming influence spread broadly, and both Yi tribesmen and Han submitted gladly.

units.zh: 秩滿將歸，群蠻追送，賂遺甚多，軫一無所受，去如初至。
units.en: As he finished his tour and prepared to go home, hill peoples trailed after him with lavish parting gifts; he took none of it and rode away as plainly as the day he came.
units.literal: When his term ended and he was about to leave, crowds of Man tribesmen followed him to see him off, offering many bribes and gifts; Zhen accepted nothing and departed as simply as when he had first arrived.

units.zh: 又除池陽令，為雍州十一郡最。
units.en: His next post was Chiyang, where his evaluation topped all eleven Yong commanderies.
units.literal: Again appointed magistrate of Chiyang, he ranked first among the eleven commanderies of Yong Province.

units.zh: 百姓生為立祠，得罪者無怨言。
units.en: Locals raised a shrine to him in his lifetime, and even convicts accepted punishment without grudge.
units.literal: The common people built a shrine to him while he still lived; those sentenced for crimes bore no complaint.

units.zh: 累遷尚書郎。
units.en: He rose through several posts to gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 軫博聞廣涉，奏議駁論多見施用。
units.en: Du Zhen was erudite; the court regularly adopted his memorials and policy debates.
units.literal: Zhen read widely; his memorials, deliberations, and rebuttals were often put into practice.

units.zh: 時涪人李驤亦為尚書郎，與軫齊名，每有論議，朝廷莫能逾之，號蜀有二郎。
units.en: Li Xiang of Fu served alongside him as gentleman of the Masters of Writing; their arguments set the standard at court, earning the nickname 'the two gentlemen of Shu.'
units.literal: At that time Li Xiang of Fu also held the post of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and matched Zhen in reputation; whenever they debated policy the court could not outdo them—they were called the Two Gentlemen of Shu.

units.zh: 軫後拜犍為太守，甚有聲譽。
units.en: He later governed Qianwei and won wide acclaim.
units.literal: Later Zhen was appointed Administrator of Qianwei and enjoyed a strong reputation.

units.zh: 當遷，會病卒，年五十一。
units.en: He was slated for promotion but died of illness at fifty-one.
units.literal: When he was due for promotion he fell ill and died, age fifty-one.

units.zh: 子毗。
units.en: His son was Du Pi.
units.literal: His son Pi.

units.zh: 軫子 毗
units.en: Du Pi (Du Zhen's son)
units.literal: Du Zhen's son Pi

units.zh: 毗字長基。
units.en: Du Pi, courtesy Changji.
units.literal: Pi, courtesy name Changji.

units.zh: 州舉秀才，成都王穎辟大將軍掾，遷尚書郎，參太傅軍事。
units.en: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he entered Prince Chengdu Sima Ying's staff as grand-general aide, then became gentleman of the Masters of Writing and adviser on the grand tutor's army council.
units.literal: The province raised him as cultivated talent; Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as aide to the grand general; he was promoted Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and joined the Grand Tutor's military staff.

units.zh: 及洛陽覆沒，毗南渡江，王敦表為益州刺史，將與宜都太守柳純共固白帝。
units.en: After the Luoyang catastrophe he fled south; Wang Dun nominated him for Yi Province so he could join Yidu prefect Liu Chun in holding Baidi.
units.literal: When Luoyang fell he crossed south of the Yangzi; Wang Dun recommended him as Inspector of Yi Province; he was to cooperate with Administrator of Yidu Liu Chun in holding Ba Di.

units.zh: 杜弢遣軍要毗，遂遇害。
units.en: The rebel Du Tao ambushed him and cut him down.
units.literal: Du Tao sent troops to intercept Pi; Pi was killed.

units.zh: 毗弟 秀
units.en: Du Xiu (younger brother of Du Pi)
units.literal: Pi's younger brother Xiu

units.zh: 毗弟秀，字彥穎，為羅尚主簿。
units.en: Du Xiu (courtesy Yanying), Du Pi's younger brother, was chief clerk to Luo Shang.
units.literal: Pi's younger brother Xiu, courtesy name Yanying, served as chief clerk to Luo Shang.

units.zh: 州沒，為氏賊李驤所得，欲用為司馬。
units.en: After the province collapsed Di warlord Li Xiang seized him and offered him the post of army marshal.
units.literal: When the province fell he was captured by the Di leader Li Xiang, who wished to employ him as marshal.

units.zh: 秀不受，見害。
units.en: Du Xiu refused and was executed.
units.literal: Xiu refused and was killed.

units.zh: 毗次子歆，舉秀才。
units.en: Du Pi's second son Du Xin passed the provincial cultivated-talent examination.
units.literal: Pi's second son Xin was raised as cultivated talent.

units.zh: 軫弟 烈
units.en: Du Lie (younger brother of Du Zhen)
units.literal: Zhen's younger brother Lie

units.zh: 軫弟烈，明政事，察孝廉，曆平康、安陽令，所居有異績，遷衡陽太守。
units.en: Du Lie, another brother of Du Zhen, excelled at governance; as filial-and-incorrupt nominee he magistrated Pingkang and Anyang with distinction, then became prefect of Hengyang.
units.literal: Zhen's younger brother Lie understood practical administration; recommended as filial and incorrupt, he served as magistrate of Pingkang and Anyang with outstanding records at each post; promoted Administrator of Hengyang.

units.zh: 聞軫亡，因自表兄子幼弱，求去官，詔轉犍為太守，蜀土榮之。
units.en: Learning of Du Zhen's death, he asked leave on the ground that his nephews were infants; the court moved him to Qianwei instead, a gesture Shu folk deeply respected.
units.literal: When he heard of Zhen's death he memorialized that his elder brother's sons were still young and weak and begged to resign; an edict transferred him to Administrator of Qianwei; the people of Shu honored him for it.

units.zh: 後遷湘東太守，為成都王穎郎中令，病卒。
units.en: He later governed Xiangdong and served as Chamberlain of the Palace Gentlemen to Prince Chengdu, then died of illness.
units.literal: Later promoted Administrator of Xiangdong, he served as Chamberlain of the Palace Attendants (langzhongling) to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; died of illness.

units.zh: 烈弟 良
units.en: Du Liang (younger brother of Du Lie)
units.literal: Lie's younger brother Liang

units.zh: 烈弟良，舉秀才，除新都令、涪陵太守，不就，補州大中正，卒。
units.en: Du Liang, Du Lie's youngest brother, passed the cultivated-talent exam and received calls to Xindu and Fuling but declined; he ended as the province's senior evaluator and died in that role.
units.literal: Liang, younger brother of Lie, was raised as cultivated talent; appointed magistrate of Xindu and Administrator of Fuling—he did not take office; appointed provincial senior evaluator; died.

units.zh: 竇允
units.en: Dou Yun
units.literal: Dou Yun

units.zh: 竇允，字雅，始平人也。
units.en: Dou Yun (courtesy Ya) came from Shiping.
units.literal: Dou Yun, courtesy name Ya, was a native of Shiping.

units.zh: 出自寒門，清尚自修。
units.en: Born to a poor household, he disciplined himself toward austerity and honor.
units.literal: He came from a humble family and cultivated purity and lofty conduct on his own.

units.zh: 少仕縣，稍遷郡主簿。
units.en: He began in county service and worked up to commandery chief clerk.
units.literal: In youth he served the county and gradually rose to chief clerk of the commandery.

units.zh: 察孝廉，除浩亹長。
units.en: As filial-and-incorrupt nominee he became magistrate of Haomen county.
units.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he was appointed magistrate of Haomen.

units.zh: 勤於為政，勸課田蠶，平均調役，百姓賴之。
units.en: He pushed farming and silk-rearing, spread levies fairly, and earned the people's trust.
units.literal: Diligent in governance, he urged farming and sericulture, equalized taxes and corvée; the common people relied on him.

units.zh: 遷謁者。
units.en: He moved up to palace usher.
units.literal: Promoted to usher.

units.zh: 泰始中，詔曰：「當官者能潔身修己，然後在公之節乃全。
units.en: In the Taishi era an edict said: 'Those who hold office must purify and cultivate themselves; only then is public integrity complete.
units.literal: In the Taishi era an edict said: 'Those who hold office must purify and cultivate themselves; only then is public integrity complete.

units.zh: 身善有章，雖賤必賞，此興化立教之務也。
units.en: When personal goodness is manifest, though the rank be low, reward must follow—this is how one promotes transforming influence and establishes instruction.
units.literal: When personal goodness is manifest, though the rank be low, reward must follow—this is how one promotes transforming influence and establishes instruction.

units.zh: 謁者竇允前為浩亹長，以修勤清白見稱河右。
units.en: Usher Dou Yun, formerly magistrate of Haomen, was praised west of the River for diligent cultivation and pure conduct.
units.literal: Usher Dou Yun, formerly magistrate of Haomen, was praised west of the River for diligent cultivation and pure conduct.

units.zh: 是輩當擢用，使立行者有所勸。
units.en: Men of this sort ought to be promoted so that those who practice upright conduct have something to strive toward.
units.literal: Men of this sort ought to be promoted so that those who practice upright conduct have something to strive toward.

units.zh: 主者詳復參訪，有以旌表之。」
units.en: Let the responsible offices examine and investigate thoroughly and issue commendations.'
units.literal: Let the responsible offices examine and investigate thoroughly and issue commendations.'

units.zh: 拜臨水令。
units.en: Dou Yun received Linshui county.
units.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Linshui.

units.zh: 克己厲俗，改修政事，士庶悅服，咸歌詠之。
units.en: He tightened his own conduct, reshaped local practice, and won scholars and farmers alike—they sang his praises.
units.literal: He restrained himself and sternly improved custom, revised administration; gentry and commoners submitted gladly and all sang his praises.

units.zh: 遷钜鹿太守，甚有政績。
units.en: Promoted to Administrator of Julu, he compiled a notable administrative record.
units.literal: Promoted Administrator of Julu; he achieved considerable administrative results.

units.zh: 卒於官。
units.en: He died in harness.
units.literal: Died in office.

units.zh: 王宏
units.en: Wang Hong
units.literal: Wang Hong

units.zh: 王宏，字正宗，高平人，魏侍中粲之從孫也。
units.en: Wang Hong (courtesy Zhengzong) of Gaoping traced his line collaterally from Wei inner-court attendant Wang Can.
units.literal: Wang Hong, courtesy name Zhengzong, was a man of Gaoping; he was a collateral descendant of Wang Can, attendant of the inner court in Wei.

units.zh: 魏時辟公府，累遷尚書郎，曆給事中。
units.en: Under Wei he was summoned to a ducal office, rose by steps to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and served as Supervising Secretary.
units.literal: In Wei he was summoned to the ministerial offices; repeatedly promoted Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; served successively as palace attendant.

units.zh: 泰始初，為汲郡太守，撫百姓如家，耕桑樹藝，屋宇阡陌，莫不躬自教示，曲盡事宜，在郡有殊績。
units.en: Early in Taishi he took Ji commandery and treated households like kin: he walked every field and lane to teach sowing, mulberry, and building until nothing essential was left undone, and his ratings soared.
units.literal: At the start of Taishi he became Administrator of Ji commandery; he treated the common people like family—plowing, mulberry, planting, houses and field paths—there was nothing he did not personally teach and demonstrate, exhaustively covering what was needful; in the commandery he achieved exceptional results.

units.zh: 司隸校尉石鑒上其政術，武帝下詔稱之曰：「朕惟人食之急，而懼天時水旱之運，夙夜警戒，念在於農。
units.en: Metropolitan Governor Shi Jian reported his administrative methods; Emperor Wu issued an edict praising him, saying: 'I consider the urgency of people's food and fear the workings of flood and drought in season; day and night I am on guard, my thoughts on agriculture.
units.literal: Metropolitan Governor Shi Jian reported his administrative methods; Emperor Wu issued an edict praising him, saying: 'I consider the urgency of people's food and fear the workings of flood and drought in season; day and night I am on guard, my thoughts on agriculture.

units.zh: 雖詔書屢下，敕厲殷勤，猶恐百姓廢惰以損生植之功。
units.en: Though edicts have been issued repeatedly and instructions earnestly urged, I still fear the common people may grow idle and lazy and impair the work of nurturing growth.
units.literal: Though edicts have been issued repeatedly and instructions earnestly urged, I still fear the common people may grow idle and lazy and impair the work of nurturing growth.

units.zh: 而刺史、二千石、百里長吏未能盡勤，至使地有遺利而人有餘力，每思聞監司糾舉能不，將行其賞罰，以明沮勸。
units.en: Yet inspectors, commandery governors of two thousand shi, and magistrates of a hundred li have not been able to do their utmost, so that the land still holds uncultivated surplus while people have leftover strength; whenever I think of this I wish to hear whether overseers report who can and who cannot, so as to apply rewards and punishments and make encouragement and discouragement clear.
units.literal: Yet inspectors, commandery governors of two thousand shi, and magistrates of a hundred li have not been able to do their utmost, so that the land still holds uncultivated surplus while people have leftover strength; whenever I think of this I wish to hear whether overseers report who can and who cannot, so as to apply rewards and punishments and make encouragement and discouragement clear.

units.zh: 今司隸校尉石鑒上汲郡太守王宏勤恤百姓，導化有方，督勸開荒五千餘頃，而熟田常課頃畝不減。
units.en: Now Metropolitan Governor Shi Jian reports that Administrator of Ji commandery Wang Hong diligently comforts the common people and guides transformation effectively; he supervised and urged the opening of more than five thousand qing of new fields while tax grain from mature fields did not decrease per mu.
units.literal: Now Metropolitan Governor Shi Jian reports that Administrator of Ji commandery Wang Hong diligently comforts the common people and guides transformation effectively; he supervised and urged the opening of more than five thousand qing of new fields while tax grain from mature fields did not decrease per mu.

units.zh: 比年普饑，人食不足，而宏郡界獨無匱乏，可謂能矣。
units.en: In recent years famine has been widespread and people lack food, yet within Hong's commandery alone there was no shortage—this may be called capable.
units.literal: In recent years famine has been widespread and people lack food, yet within Hong's commandery alone there was no shortage—this may be called capable.

units.zh: 其賜宏穀千斛，佈告天下，咸使聞知。」
units.en: Grant Hong one thousand hu of grain; proclaim this throughout the realm so all may hear and know.'
units.literal: Grant Hong one thousand hu of grain; proclaim this throughout the realm so all may hear and know.'

units.zh: 俄遷衛尉、河南尹、大司農，無復能名，更為苛碎。
units.en: Soon he was promoted Commandant of the Guards, Intendant of Henan, and Minister of Agriculture, but he no longer had a reputation for capability and became harsh and fussy.
units.literal: Shortly he was promoted Commandant of the Guards, Intendant of Henan, and Minister of Agriculture—but he no longer had his former reputation and became harsh and fussy.

units.zh: 坐桎梏罪人，以泥墨塗面，置深坑中，餓不與食，又擅縱五歲刑以下二十一人，為有司所劾。
units.en: He shackled prisoners, smeared mud on their faces, dropped them in pits, starved them, and illegally freed twenty-one convicts serving five years or less—the ministries impeached him.
units.literal: For putting convicts in cangues, smearing their faces with mud, placing them in deep pits, starving them without food, and furthermore illegally releasing twenty-one persons sentenced to five years or less, he was impeached by the relevant offices.

units.zh: 帝以宏累有政績，聽以贖罪論。
units.en: The emperor credited his earlier record and let him buy off the charge.
units.literal: The emperor, because Hong had repeatedly had administrative achievements, permitted him to redeem the offense with a fine.

units.zh: 太康中，代劉毅為司隸校尉，於是檢察士庶，使車服異制，庶人不得衣紫絳及綺繡錦繢。
units.en: Under Taikang he succeeded Liu Yi as metropolitan governor and regulated dress for nobles and commoners—common people could not wear purple, red, brocade, or figured silk.
units.literal: In Taikang he replaced Liu Yi as Metropolitan Governor; thereupon he inspected gentry and commoners, making carriage and dress follow different regulations—commoners might not wear purple, crimson, brocade embroidery, or patterned silk.

units.zh: 帝常遣左右微行，觀察風俗，宏緣此復遣吏科檢婦人衵服，至褰發于路。
units.en: The sovereign habitually sent plain-clothes agents to gauge morals; Hong sent clerks after women's under-robes and even had garments lifted in the street.
units.literal: The emperor often sent attendants incognito to observe customs; Hong on this account again sent clerks to inspect women's under-jackets, to the point of lifting skirts on the road.

units.zh: 論者以為暮年謬妄，由是獲譏於世，復坐免官。
units.en: Observers wrote him off as a foolish old man; ridicule followed and he was cashiered again.
units.literal: Critics thought him senile and absurd in his later years; on this account he was mocked by the world and again removed from office for the offense.

units.zh: 後起為尚書。
units.en: He later returned as a masters-of-writing minister.
units.literal: Later he was raised up as Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 永嘉三年，暴疾而卒，臨終歎曰：「此乃天亡冀州，豈吾命哉！」
units.en: In the third year of Yongjia, he died of a sudden illness. At the end he sighed, "This is Heaven destroying Jizhou; how could it be my fate!"
units.literal: In the third year of Yongjia, he died of a sudden illness. At the end he sighed, "This is Heaven destroying Jizhou; how could it be my fate!"

units.zh: 曹攄
units.en: Cao Shu
units.literal: Cao Shu

units.zh: 曹攄，字顏遠，譙國譙人也。
units.en: Cao Shu (courtesy Yanyuan) came from Qiao in the Qiao princedom.
units.literal: Cao Shu, courtesy name Yanyuan, was a native of Qiao in the Principality of Qiao.

units.zh: 祖肇，魏衛將軍。
units.en: His grandfather Cao Zhao had been Wei General of the Guards.
units.literal: His grandfather Zhao was Wei General of the Guards.

units.zh: 攄少有孝行，好學善屬文，太尉王衍見而器之，調補臨淄令。
units.en: Filial from boyhood, bookish and eloquent, he impressed grand commandant Wang Yan, who moved him to magistrate of Linzi.
units.literal: Shu from youth showed filial conduct, loved learning and was skilled at composition; Grand Commandant Wang Yan saw him and esteemed him; he was transferred and appointed magistrate of Linzi.

units.zh: 縣有寡婦，養姑甚謹。
units.en: The county had a widow who nursed her mother-in-law devotedly.
units.literal: In the county was a widow who tended her mother-in-law very carefully.

units.zh: 姑以其年少，勸令改適，婦守節不移。
units.en: The elder, pitying her youth, urged her to remarry; the widow refused to abandon her vow.
units.literal: The mother-in-law, because she was young, urged her to remarry; the woman kept her chastity and would not move.

units.zh: 姑湣之，密自殺。
units.en: The mother-in-law, heartsick for her, committed suicide in secret.
units.literal: The mother-in-law pitied her and secretly killed herself.

units.zh: 親党告婦殺姑，官為考鞫，寡婦不勝苦楚，乃自誣。
units.en: Kin accused the widow of murder; torture broke her and she confessed to a crime she did not commit.
units.literal: Relatives reported the woman had killed her mother-in-law; officials interrogated her under torture; the widow could not endure the pain and falsely confessed.

units.zh: 獄當決，適值攄到。
units.en: Sentence was about to fall when Cao Shu took office.
units.literal: When the case was to be decided, it happened that Shu arrived.

units.zh: 攄知其有冤，更加辯究，具得情實，時稱其明。
units.en: He sensed a miscarriage, reopened the file, and extracted the truth; contemporaries praised his insight.
units.literal: Shu knew there was injustice and investigated further; he obtained the full truth of the situation; he was at the time praised for his clarity.

units.zh: 獄有死囚，歲夕，攄行獄，湣之，曰：「卿等不幸致此非所，如何？
units.en: In the jail were condemned prisoners; at year's end Shu inspected the prison and pitied them, saying: 'You have unfortunately come to this place—what can be done?
units.literal: In the jail were condemned prisoners; at year's end Shu inspected the prison and pitied them, saying: 'You have unfortunately come to this place—what can be done?

units.zh: 新歲人情所重，豈不欲暫見家邪？」
units.en: New Year's is what human feelings most treasure—do you not wish briefly to see your families?'
units.literal: New Year's is what human feelings most treasure—do you not wish briefly to see your families?'

units.zh: 眾囚皆涕泣曰：「若得暫歸，死無恨也。」
units.en: All the prisoners wept and said: 'If we could return for a little while, we would die without regret.'
units.literal: All the prisoners wept and said: 'If we could return for a little while, we would die without regret.'

units.zh: 攄悉開獄出之，克日令還。
units.en: He threw open the gates, freed them all, and named the day they must return.
units.literal: Shu opened all the prisons and released them, setting a deadline for their return.

units.zh: 掾吏固爭，咸謂不可。
units.en: His aides protested that the risk was insane.
units.literal: The clerks firmly objected, all saying it could not be done.

units.zh: 攄曰：「此雖小人，義不見負，自為諸君任之。」
units.en: Shu said: 'Though these are petty men, in honor they will not betray me; I myself answer for them to you gentlemen.'
units.literal: Shu said: 'Though these are petty men, in honor they will not betray me; I myself answer for them to you gentlemen.'

units.zh: 至日，相率而還，並無違者，一縣嘆服，號曰聖君。
units.en: Every man returned on time; the county hailed him as a sage official.
units.literal: When the day came they came back together; none broke the promise—the whole county marveled and submitted, calling him the sage lord.

units.zh: 入為尚書郎，轉洛陽令，仁惠明斷，百姓懷之。
units.en: He reached the Masters of Writing and then Luoyang county—kind, sharp, and beloved.
units.literal: He entered [court] as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, transferred to magistrate of Luoyang; benevolent, kind, and clear in judgment—the common people cherished him.

units.zh: 時天大雨雪，宮門夜失行馬，群官檢察，莫知所在。
units.en: One night of blizzard the palace gate's traveling barriers vanished; no search turned them up.
units.literal: At that time heaven sent great rain and snow; at night the traveling barriers at the palace gate were lost; the various officials searched and none knew where they were.

units.zh: 攄使收門士，眾官咸謂不然。
units.en: Cao Shu arrested the gate guards; colleagues called it nonsense.
units.literal: Shu ordered the gate guards seized; all the officials said it was wrong.

units.zh: 攄曰：「宮掖禁嚴，非外人所敢盜，必是門士以燎寒耳。」
units.en: Shu said: 'The palace is strictly forbidden—outsiders would not dare steal them; it must be the gate guards taking them to warm themselves by fire.'
units.literal: Shu said: 'The palace is strictly forbidden—outsiders would not dare steal them; it must be the gate guards taking them to warm themselves by fire.'

units.zh: 詰之，果服。
units.en: Questioning proved him right.
units.literal: When questioned, they indeed confessed.

units.zh: 以病去官。
units.en: Illness forced him out.
units.literal: He left office due to illness.

units.zh: 復為洛陽令。
units.en: Luoyang eventually recalled him.
units.literal: Again became magistrate of Luoyang.

units.zh: 及齊王冏輔政，攄與左思俱為記室督。
units.en: When Prince Qi Sima Jiong directed the regime, Cao Shu and Zuo Si jointly supervised the secretariat.
units.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong assisted the government, Shu together with Zuo Si both served as supervisors of the secretariat.

units.zh: 冏嘗從容問攄曰：「天子為賊臣所逼，莫有能奮。
units.en: Jiong once calmly asked Shu: 'The Son of Heaven was coerced by traitorous ministers; none could rouse himself.
units.literal: Jiong once calmly asked Shu: 'The Son of Heaven was coerced by traitorous ministers; none could rouse himself.

units.zh: 吾率四海義兵興復王室，今入輔朝廷，匡振時艱，或有勸吾還國，於卿意如何？」
units.en: I led righteous troops from within the four seas to restore the royal house; now I enter and assist the court, aiding the hardship of the times—some urge me to return to my princedom; what is your thought?'
units.literal: I led righteous troops from within the four seas to restore the royal house; now I enter and assist the court, aiding the hardship of the times—some urge me to return to my princedom; what is your thought?'

units.zh: 攄曰：「蕩平國賊，匡復帝祚，古今人臣之功未有如大王之盛也。
units.en: Shu said: 'Sweeping away state rebels and restoring the imperial throne—among ministers through history none has achieved merit as great as the great king's.
units.literal: Shu said: 'Sweeping away state rebels and restoring the imperial throne—among ministers through history none has achieved merit as great as the great king's.

units.zh: 然道罔隆而不殺，物無盛而不衰，非唯人事，抑亦天理。
units.en: Yet the Way never rises without decline; nothing flourishes without fading—not only in human affairs but also in the pattern of Heaven.
units.literal: Yet the Way never rises without decline; nothing flourishes without fading—not only in human affairs but also in the pattern of Heaven.

units.zh: 竊預下問，敢不盡情。
units.en: Having received your humble inquiry below, how dare I not speak my whole mind.
units.literal: Having received your humble inquiry below, how dare I not speak my whole mind.

units.zh: 願大王居高慮危，在盈思沖，精選百官，存公屏欲，舉賢進善，務得其才，然後脂車秣馬，高揖歸籓，則上下同慶，攄等幸甚。」
units.en: I wish the great king, dwelling high, to think of peril; in fullness to think of emptiness; carefully select the hundred officials; preserve impartiality and restrain desire; promote the worthy and advance the good, striving to obtain true talent—then grease the carriage and feed the horses, bow deeply and return to your fief; then high and low alike will rejoice, and Shu and the rest will be greatly fortunate.'
units.literal: I wish the great king, dwelling high, to think of peril; in fullness to think of emptiness; carefully select the hundred officials; preserve impartiality and restrain desire; promote the worthy and advance the good, striving to obtain true talent—then grease the carriage and feed the horses, bow deeply and return to your fief; then high and low alike will rejoice, and Shu and the rest will be greatly fortunate.'

units.zh: 冏不納。
units.en: Sima Jiong brushed the counsel aside.
units.literal: Jiong did not accept the advice.

units.zh: 尋轉中書侍郎。
units.en: He soon moved to vice director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Shortly he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 長沙王乂以為驃騎司馬。
units.en: Prince Changsha Sima Yi named him staff marshal on the agile-cavalry command.
units.literal: Prince Changsha Sima Yi appointed him marshal for the General of Agile Cavalry.

units.zh: 乂敗，免官。
units.en: After Prince Changsha fell, Cao Shu lost his post.
units.literal: When Yi was defeated, [Shu] was dismissed from office.

units.zh: 因丁母憂。
units.en: He then withdrew to mourn his mother.
units.literal: Thereupon he observed mourning for his mother.

units.zh: 惠帝末，起為襄城太守，
units.en: Late in Emperor Hui's reign he returned as Xiangcheng prefect.
units.literal: At the end of Emperor Hui's reign he was raised up as Administrator of Xiangcheng.

units.zh: 永嘉二年，高密王簡鎮襄陽，以攄為征南司馬。
units.en: In the second year of Yongjia, Prince Gaomi Sima Jian, commanding Xiangyang, put Cao Shu in charge of the southern army staff.
units.literal: In the second year of Yongjia, Prince of Gaomi Sima Jian was stationed at Xiangyang and appointed Shu as marshal for the southern expedition.

units.zh: 其年流人王逌等聚眾屯冠軍，寇掠城邑。
units.en: Refugee bands under Wang You encamped at Guanjun that year and looted cities along the way.
units.literal: That year displaced persons led by Wang You and others gathered at Guanjun, raiding towns.

units.zh: 簡遣參軍崔曠討之，令攄督護曠。
units.en: Sima Jian dispatched Cui Kuang to attack them while Cao Shu oversaw Kuang as protector.
units.literal: Jian sent adjutant Cui Kuang against them and ordered Shu to supervise Kuang.

units.zh: 曠，奸凶人也，譎攄前戰，期為後繼，既而不至。
units.en: Cui Kuang was treacherous: he pushed Cao Shu forward and promised support that never arrived.
units.literal: Kuang was a treacherous man; he tricked Shu into taking the front line, promising reinforcements, then never came.

units.zh: 攄獨與逌戰於酈縣，軍敗死之。
units.en: Cao Shu met Wang You near Li county alone, lost the battle, and was killed.
units.literal: Shu alone fought Wang You at Li county; his force was routed and he died.

units.zh: 故吏及百姓並奔喪會葬，號哭即路，如赴父母焉。
units.en: Old aides and ordinary folk raced to his funeral, weeping in the street as for a parent.
units.literal: Former subordinates and common people alike hurried to mourning and funeral gatherings; they wailed along the road as if burying parents.

units.zh: 潘京
units.en: Pan Jing
units.literal: Pan Jing

units.zh: 潘京，字世長，武陵漢壽人也。
units.en: Pan Jing (courtesy Shichang) came from Hanshou in Wuling commandery.
units.literal: Pan Jing, courtesy name Shichang, was a native of Hanshou in Wuling.

units.zh: 弱冠，郡辟主簿，太守趙廞甚器之，嘗問曰：「貴郡何以名武陵？」
units.en: At the capping age the commandery summoned him as chief clerk; Administrator Zhao Xin esteemed him highly and once asked: "Why is your commandery called Wuling?"
units.literal: At the capping age the commandery summoned him as chief clerk; Administrator Zhao Xin esteemed him highly and once asked: "Why is your commandery called Wuling?"

units.zh: 京曰：「鄙郡本名義陵，在辰陽縣界，與夷相接，數為所攻，光武時移東出，遂得全完，共議易號。
units.en: Jing replied: "Our commandery was originally Yiling, within Chenyang county; it bordered the Yi tribes and suffered repeated attacks; in Emperor Guangwu's reign it was shifted eastward and survived intact; the elders then chose a new name.
units.literal: Jing replied: "Our commandery was originally Yiling, within Chenyang county; it bordered the Yi tribes and suffered repeated attacks; in Emperor Guangwu's reign it was shifted eastward and survived intact; the elders then chose a new name.

units.zh: 《傳》曰止戈為武，《詩》稱高平曰陵，於是名焉。」
units.en: The Documents says 'stopping weapons is martial'; the Odes calls a high, peaceful land a "mound"; hence the new name."
units.literal: The Documents says 'stopping weapons is martial'; the Odes calls a high, peaceful land a "mound"; hence the new name."

units.zh: 為州所辟，因謁見問策，探得「不孝」字，刺史戲京曰：「辟士為不孝邪？」
units.en: Summoned by the province, at audience he drew lots for a policy question and received the pair 'unfilial'; the inspector teased Jing: "Are you summoning a man who is unfilial?"
units.literal: Summoned by the province, at audience he drew lots for a policy question and received the pair 'unfilial'; the inspector teased Jing: "Are you summoning a man who is unfilial?"

units.zh: 京舉版答曰：「今為忠臣，不得復為孝子。」
units.en: Jing lifted his writing tablet and answered: "Today I am a loyal subject; I cannot also be a filial son."
units.literal: Jing lifted his writing tablet and answered: "Today I am a loyal subject; I cannot also be a filial son."

units.zh: 其機辯皆此類。
units.en: His repartee ran in that vein.
units.literal: His ready wit was always of this kind.

units.zh: 後太廟立，州郡皆遣使賀，京白太守曰：「夫太廟立，移神主，應問訊，不應賀。」
units.en: Later, when the Grand Ancestral Temple was completed, every province and commandery sent envoys to congratulate; Jing told the administrator: "When the temple is dedicated and spirit tablets move, the court deserves condolence, not cheering."
units.literal: Later, when the Grand Ancestral Temple was completed, every province and commandery sent envoys to congratulate; Jing told the administrator: "When the temple is dedicated and spirit tablets move, the court deserves condolence, not cheering."

units.zh: 遂遣京作文，使詣京師，以為永式。
units.en: He then had Jing compose a text and sent him to the capital, taking it as the permanent precedent.
units.literal: Thereupon he had Jing compose a memorial and sent it to the capital as the permanent precedent.

units.zh: 京仍舉秀才，到洛。
units.en: Recommended again as cultivated talent, he went to Luoyang.
units.literal: Jing was again raised as cultivated talent and traveled to Luoyang.

units.zh: 尚書令樂廣，京州人也，共談累日，深歎其才，謂京曰：「君天才過人，恨不學耳。
units.en: Masters of Writing chief Yue Guang, a fellow townsman, talked with him for days, marveled at his gifts, and said: "Your genius surpasses others; I only regret you have not studied.
units.literal: Masters of Writing chief Yue Guang, a fellow townsman, talked with him for days, marveled at his gifts, and said: "Your genius surpasses others; I only regret you have not studied.

units.zh: 若學，必為一代談宗。」
units.en: If you studied, you would surely become this age's master of pure conversation."
units.literal: If you studied, you would surely become this age's master of pure conversation."

units.zh: 京感其言，遂勤學不倦。
units.en: Pan Jing took the hint and studied without slackening.
units.literal: Jing was moved by his words and thereupon studied tirelessly.

units.zh: 時武陵太守戴昌亦善談論，與京共談，京假借之，昌以為不如己，笑而遣之，令過其子若思，京方極其言論。
units.en: Administrator Dai Chang of Wuling also loved Pure Talk; when he sparred with Jing, Jing humored him; Chang thought himself superior, laughed him off, and sent him to debate his son Ruosi—only then did Jing unfurl his full argument.
units.literal: Administrator Dai Chang of Wuling also loved Pure Talk; when he sparred with Jing, Jing humored him; Chang thought himself superior, laughed him off, and sent him to debate his son Ruosi—only then did Jing unfurl his full argument.

units.zh: 昌竊聽之，乃嘆服曰：「才不可假。」
units.en: Chang listened in secret and sighed: "Talent cannot be borrowed."
units.literal: Chang listened in secret and sighed: "Talent cannot be borrowed."

units.zh: 遂父子俱屈焉。
units.en: Father and son both yielded the point.
units.literal: Thereupon father and son both conceded.

units.zh: 曆巴丘、邵陵、泉陵三令。
units.en: He magistrated Baqiu, Shaoling, and Quanling in turn.
units.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Baqiu, Shaoling, and Quanling.

units.zh: 京明於政術，路不拾遺。
units.en: His administration ran so honestly that no one picked up lost property.
units.literal: Jing was clear in governing technique; lost goods lay untouched on the roads.

units.zh: 遷桂林太守，不就，歸家，年五十卒。
units.en: Called to Guilin, he declined, retired, and died at fifty.
units.literal: Promoted Administrator of Guilin—he did not take office, returned home, and died at fifty.

units.zh: 范晷
units.en: Fan Gui
units.literal: Fan Gui

units.zh: 范晷，字彥長，南陽順陽人也。
units.en: Fan Gui (courtesy Yanchang) came from Shunyang in Nanyang.
units.literal: Fan Gui, courtesy name Yanchang, was a native of Shunyang in Nanyang.

units.zh: 少遊學清河，遂徙家僑居。
units.en: He studied in Qinghe as a youth and moved his family there.
units.literal: In youth he studied in Qinghe and then relocated his household there as a sojourner.

units.zh: 郡命為五官掾，曆河內郡丞。
units.en: The commandery gave him the five-bureaus clerkship; he became assistant administrator of Henei.
units.literal: The commandery appointed him clerk of the five offices; he served as assistant administrator of Henei.

units.zh: 太守裴楷雅知之，薦為侍御史。
units.en: Prefect Pei Kai admired him and nominated him attendant censor.
units.literal: Administrator Pei Kai esteemed him and recommended him as attendant censor.

units.zh: 調補上谷太守，遭喪，不之官。
units.en: Ordered to Shanggu, he stayed home mourning instead.
units.literal: Transferred to Administrator of Shanggu; he met bereavement and did not take up the post.

units.zh: 後為司徒左長史，轉馮翊太守，甚有政能，善於綏撫，百姓愛悅之。
units.en: He advanced to senior clerk under the minister of education, then governed Pingyi with strong relief efforts and popular affection.
units.literal: Later he became senior clerk of the left to the Minister of Education, transferred to Administrator of Pingyi—very capable in administration, skilled at pacification; the people loved him.

units.zh: 徵拜少府，出為涼州刺史，轉雍州。
units.en: The court called him privy treasurer, then sent him west as Liang inspector and Yong inspector.
units.literal: Summoned as Privy Treasurer; went out as Inspector of Liang Province, transferred to Yong Province.

units.zh: 于時西土荒毀，氏羌蹈藉，田桑失收，百姓困弊，晷傾心化導，勸以農桑，所部甚賴之。
units.en: The northwest was shattered by Di and Qiang raids and crop failure; Fan Gui preached farming and care until the region stabilized.
units.literal: At that time the western regions lay in ruins; Di and Qiang rampaged; harvests failed; the people were desperate; Gui devoted himself to moral suasion, urging farming and silk; his jurisdictions depended on him.

units.zh: 元康中，加左將軍，卒于官。
units.en: Under Yuankang he added General of the Left and died in harness.
units.literal: In the Yuankang era he was additionally appointed General of the Left and died in office.

units.zh: 二子：廣、稚。
units.en: He left two sons, Guang and Zhi.
units.literal: Two sons: Guang and Zhi.

units.zh: 晷子 廣
units.en: Fan Guang (Fan Gui's son)
units.literal: Gui's son Guang

units.zh: 廣字仲將。
units.en: Fan Guang, courtesy Zhongjiang.
units.literal: Guang, courtesy name Zhongjiang.

units.zh: 舉孝廉，除靈壽令，不之官。
units.en: Recommended filial and incorrupt for Lingshou, he never took the post.
units.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt; appointed magistrate of Lingshou—he did not take office.

units.zh: 姊適孫氏，早亡，有孫名邁，廣負以南奔，雖盜賊艱急，終不棄之。
units.en: His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a son named Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.
units.literal: His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a son named Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.

units.zh: 元帝承制，以為堂邑令。
units.en: Emperor Yuan's provisional regime named him magistrate of Tangyi.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan, exercising interim authority, appointed him magistrate of Tangyi.

units.zh: 丞劉榮坐事當死，郡劾以付縣。
units.en: Assistant Liu Rong faced capital charges; the prefect sent him down to the county jail.
units.literal: Assistant magistrate Liu Rong faced execution for an offense; the commandery impeached him and remanded him to the county.

units.zh: 榮即縣人，家有老母，至節，廣輒聽暫還，榮亦如期而反。
units.en: Liu was a local with an elderly mother; Fan Guang released him for holidays and he always returned on time.
units.literal: Rong was a local man with an aged mother; at festivals Guang always let him visit home briefly; Rong returned on schedule.

units.zh: 縣堂為野火所及，榮脫械救火，事畢，還自著械。
units.en: When brush fire threatened the yamen, Liu slipped his chains to fight the flames, then refastened himself.
units.literal: The county hall caught fire from a brush blaze; Rong slipped his fetters to fight the fire; when done he locked himself again.

units.zh: 後大旱，米貴，廣散私穀振饑人，至數千斛，遠近流寓歸投之，戶口十倍。
units.en: During famine he fed thousands of hu from his own granaries; refugees poured in and his county rolls swelled tenfold.
units.literal: Later came great drought and dear grain; Guang distributed thousands of hu of his private grain to the starving; displaced people flocked in until registered households multiplied tenfold.

units.zh: 卒於官。
units.en: He died in office.
units.literal: Died in office.

units.zh: 晷子 稚
units.en: Fan Zhi (Fan Gui's son)
units.literal: Gui's son Zhi

units.zh: 稚少知名，辟大將軍掾，早卒。
units.en: Fan Zhi won early fame, joined the grand general's staff, and died young.
units.literal: Zhi was known from youth; summoned as aide to the grand general; died young.

units.zh: 子汪，別有傳。
units.en: His son Fan Wang has his own biography elsewhere.
units.literal: His son Wang has a separate biography.

units.zh: 丁紹
units.en: Ding Shao
units.literal: Ding Shao

units.zh: 丁紹，字叔倫，譙國人也。
units.en: Ding Shao (courtesy Shulun) came from the Qiao princedom.
units.literal: Ding Shao, courtesy name Shulun, was a native of the Principality of Qiao.

units.zh: 少開朗公正，早曆清官，為廣平太守，政平訟理，道化大行。
units.en: Cheerful and fair in youth, he rose through unsullied posts; at Guangping justice ran straight and instruction spread wide.
units.literal: In youth he was open, forthright, and just; early he served in pure posts; as Administrator of Guangping, government was even and lawsuits were clear; transforming guidance spread broadly.

units.zh: 于時河北騷擾，靡有完邑，而廣平一郡四境乂安，是以皆悅其法而從其令。
units.en: While Hebei burned and every other county shattered, Guangping stayed calm; people welcomed his code.
units.literal: At that time north of the Yellow River was in turmoil and no district stood intact, yet Guangping alone enjoyed peace on every border; therefore all rejoiced in his laws and obeyed his commands.

units.zh: 及臨漳被圍，南陽王模窘急，紹率郡兵赴之，模賴以獲全。
units.en: When Linzhang was invested and Prince Nanyang Sima Mo was trapped, Ding Shao marched county troops and saved him.
units.literal: When Linzhang was besieged, Prince of Nanyang Sima Mo was desperate; Shao led commandery troops to his rescue; Mo survived thanks to him.

units.zh: 模感紹恩，生為立碑。
units.en: Sima Mo was so grateful he raised a stele to Ding Shao during his lifetime.
units.literal: Mo, grateful for Shao's kindness, erected a stele for him while Shao still lived.

units.zh: 遷徐州刺史，士庶戀慕，攀附如歸。
units.en: Promoted to Xu inspector, he drew scholars and commoners who clung to him like kin.
units.literal: Promoted Inspector of Xu Province; gentry and commoners clung to him, attaching themselves as if coming home.

units.zh: 未之官，復轉荊州刺史。
units.en: He never reached Xu—the court shifted him to Jing inspector.
units.literal: Before he reached his post he was again transferred Inspector of Jing Province.

units.zh: 從車千乘，南渡河至許。
units.en: A thousand-car entourage forded the river toward Xu.
units.literal: A train of a thousand carts crossed the Yellow River south to Xu.

units.zh: 時南陽王模為都督，留紹，啟轉為冀州刺史。
units.en: Area commander Sima Mo kept him and arranged a Ji inspector posting instead.
units.literal: At that time Prince of Nanyang Sima Mo was area commander; he detained Shao and petitioned to transfer him to Inspector of Ji Province.

units.zh: 到鎮，率州兵討破汲桑有功，加甯北將軍、假節、監冀州諸軍事。
units.en: On station he crushed Ji Sang's bandits and earned General Who Pacifies the North with credentials over Ji.
units.literal: Upon reaching his command he led provincial troops, defeated Ji Sang with merit, and was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the North with credentials, supervising Ji military affairs.

units.zh: 時境內羯賊為患，紹捕而誅之，號為嚴肅，河北人畏而愛之。
units.en: He hunted Jie marauders ruthlessly; northerners feared and respected his severity.
units.literal: At that time Jie bandits plagued the territory; Shao captured and executed them; he was deemed stern; people north of the Yellow River feared and loved him.

units.zh: 紹自以為才足為物雄，當官蒞政，每事克舉，視天下之事若運於掌握，遂慨然有董正四海之志矣。
units.en: He fancied himself master of the moment—every policy worked—and dreamed of rectifying the empire.
units.literal: Shao believed his talent could dominate the age; in office he succeeded at every task; seeing all under heaven as moved in his palm, he aspired to reorder the realm.

units.zh: 是時王浚盛于幽州，苟晞盛於青州，然紹視二人蔑如也，
units.en: Wang Jun ruled You and Gou Xi ruled Qing, yet Ding Shao sneered at both.
units.literal: At this time Wang Jun flourished in Youzhou and Gou Xi flourished in Qingzhou, yet Shao treated both with contempt.

units.zh: 暴疾而卒，臨終歎曰：「此乃天亡冀州，豈吾命哉！」
units.en: He suddenly died of a violent illness; facing death he sighed: "This is Heaven destroying Ji Province—how could it be my fate alone!"
units.literal: He suddenly died of a violent illness; facing death he sighed: "This is Heaven destroying Ji Province—how could it be my fate alone!"

units.zh: 懷帝策贈車騎將軍。
units.en: Emperor Huai posthumously named him general of chariots and cavalry.
units.literal: Emperor Huai posthumously appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry by edict.

units.zh: 喬智明
units.en: Qiao Zhiming
units.literal: Qiao Zhiming

units.zh: 喬智明，字元達，鮮卑前部人也。
units.en: Qiao Zhiming (courtesy Yuanda) belonged to the forward wing of the Xianbei confederation.
units.literal: Qiao Zhiming, courtesy name Yuanda, was a man of the forward division of the Xianbei.

units.zh: 少喪二親，哀毀過禮，長而以德行著稱。
units.en: Orphaned young, he mourned beyond ritual and matured renowned for character.
units.literal: In youth he lost both parents; his grief exceeded ritual propriety; grown, he was famed for virtuous conduct.

units.zh: 成都王穎辟為輔國將軍。
units.en: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying appointed him General Who Supports the State.
units.literal: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as General Who Supports the State.

units.zh: 穎之敗趙王倫也，表智明為殄寇將軍、隆慮、共二縣令。
units.en: After defeating Prince Zhao Sima Lun, Sima Ying named him General Who Exterminates Brigands and magistrate of Longlu and Gong.
units.literal: When Ying defeated Prince Zhao Sima Lun, he memorialized Zhiming as General Who Exterminates Brigands and magistrate of Longlu and Gong counties.

units.zh: 二縣愛之，號為「神君」。
units.en: Both counties loved him; they called him the "divine magistrate."
units.literal: Both counties loved him; they called him the "divine magistrate."

units.zh: 部人張兌為父報仇，母老單身，有妻無子，智明湣之，停其獄。
units.en: Commoner Zhang Dui killed for vengeance; his mother lived alone and he lacked an heir; Qiao Zhiming stayed judgment out of mercy.
units.literal: A local man Zhang Dui avenged his father; his mother was old and lived alone; he had a wife but no son; Zhiming pitied him and stayed the case.

units.zh: 歲餘，令兌將妻入獄，兼陰縱之。
units.en: After a year he let Zhang bring his wife into custody and quietly allowed intimacy.
units.literal: After more than a year he ordered Dui to bring his wife into jail and secretly allowed conjugal visits.

units.zh: 人有勸兌逃者，兌曰：「有君如此，吾何忍累之！
units.en: Someone urged Dui to flee; Dui said: "With a magistrate like this, how could I bear to drag him down!
units.literal: Someone urged Dui to flee; Dui said: "With a magistrate like this, how could I bear to drag him down!

units.zh: 縱吾得免，作何面目視息世間！」
units.en: Even if I could escape, what face would I have to face the world and breathe!"
units.literal: Even if I could escape, what face would I have to face the world and breathe!"

units.zh: 於獄產一男。
units.en: His wife delivered a son in prison.
units.literal: In the jail his wife bore a boy.

units.zh: 會赦，得免。
units.en: An amnesty freed him.
units.literal: An amnesty arrived and he obtained release.

units.zh: 其仁感如是。
units.en: Such was the power of his humane rule.
units.literal: His humane kindness moved people thus.

units.zh: 惠帝之伐鄴也，穎以智明為折沖將軍、參丞相前鋒軍事。
units.en: During Emperor Hui's expedition against Ye, Sima Ying made him General Who Charges the Enemy on the vanguard staff.
units.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned against Ye, Ying appointed Zhiming General Who Charges the Enemy and adjutant on the prime minister's vanguard staff.

units.zh: 智明勸穎奉迎乘輿，穎大怒曰：「卿名曉事，投身事孤。
units.en: Zhiming urged Ying to welcome the emperor's carriage; Ying raged: "Your reputation says you understand affairs—yet you entered my service.
units.literal: Zhiming urged Ying to welcome the emperor's carriage; Ying raged: "Your reputation says you understand affairs—yet you entered my service.

units.zh: 主上為群小所逼，將加非罪於孤，卿奈何欲使孤束手就刑邪！
units.en: The sovereign was forced by petty men and will heap false crimes on me—why would you have me bind my hands for execution!
units.literal: The sovereign was forced by petty men and will heap false crimes on me—why would you have me bind my hands for execution!

units.zh: 共事之義，正若此乎？」
units.en: Is comradeship supposed to mean this?"
units.literal: Is comradeship supposed to mean this?"

units.zh: 智明乃止。
units.en: Qiao Zhiming fell silent.
units.literal: Zhiming thereupon desisted.

units.zh: 尋屬永嘉之亂，仕于劉曜。
units.en: When Yongjia chaos erupted he entered Liu Yao's Han-Zhao regime.
units.literal: Soon the Yongjia turmoil came; he served Liu Yao.

units.zh: 鄧攸
units.en: Deng You
units.literal: Deng You

units.zh: 鄧攸，字伯道，平陽襄陵人也。
units.en: Deng You (courtesy Bodao) came from Xiangling in Pingyang.
units.literal: Deng You, courtesy name Bodao, was a native of Xiangling in Pingyang.

units.zh: 祖殷，亮直強正。
units.en: His grandfather Deng Yin was blunt and incorruptible.
units.literal: His grandfather Yin was upright, frank, and uncompromising.

units.zh: 鐘會伐蜀，奇其才，自黽池令召為主簿。
units.en: Zhong Hui's campaign against Shu spotted his talent and pulled him from Mengchi magistrate to chief clerk.
