units.literal: When Zhong Hui campaigned against Shu, he marveled at his talent and summoned him from magistrate of Mengchi to chief clerk.

units.zh: 賈充伐吳，請殷為長史。
units.en: Jia Chong's Wu expedition drafted Deng Yin as senior clerk.
units.literal: When Jia Chong campaigned against Wu, he requested Yin as senior clerk.

units.zh: 後授皇太子《詩》，為淮南太守。
units.en: He tutored the heir apparent in the Classic of Odes and took the Huainan prefecture.
units.literal: Later he instructed the crown prince in the Odes and became Administrator of Huainan.

units.zh: 夢行水邊，見一女子，猛獸自後斷其盤囊。
units.en: He dreamed of walking waterside: a woman appeared and a beast tore his belt pouch from behind.
units.literal: He dreamed he walked beside water and saw a woman; a fierce beast from behind severed his belt pouch.

units.zh: 占者以為水邊有女，汝字也，斷盤囊者，新獸頭代故獸頭也，不作汝陰，當汝南也。
units.en: Dream readers said water plus maiden spelled Ru; swapping pouch ornaments meant a new seal—expect Runan, not Runyin.
units.literal: The diviner said: beside water is a woman—that forms the character 'Ru'; severing the belt pouch means a new beast-head replaces the old; you will not go to Runyin but to Runan.

units.zh: 果遷汝陰太守。
units.en: He was posted to Runyin after all.
units.literal: Indeed he was transferred Administrator of Runyin.

units.zh: 後為中庶子。
units.en: He rose to palace attendant for the heir.
units.literal: Later he became attendant of the crown prince's household.

units.zh: 攸七歲喪父，尋喪母及祖母，居喪九年，以孝致稱。
units.en: Orphaned at seven, he buried mother and grandmother in turn and mourned nine years—a model of filial grief.
units.literal: You at age seven lost his father; soon after he lost mother and grandmother; observing mourning nine years, he was famed for filial devotion.

units.zh: 清和平簡，貞正寡欲。
units.en: Calm, modest, and spare in appetite—honest and detached.
units.literal: Pure, peaceful, plain and simple; chaste, upright, with few desires.

units.zh: 少孤，與弟同居。
units.en: Fatherless early, he kept house with his brother.
units.literal: Orphaned young, he lived with his younger brother.

units.zh: 初，祖父殷有賜官，敕攸受之。
units.en: His grandfather Yin's ennoblement had passed down by edict to Deng You.
units.literal: Originally his grandfather Yin had been granted an official patent; an edict ordered You to accept it.

units.zh: 後太守勸攸去王官，欲舉為孝廉，攸曰：「先人所賜，不可改也。」
units.en: Later the administrator urged You to surrender the royal patent so he could be raised as filial and incorrupt; You said: 'What forebears granted cannot be altered.'
units.literal: Later the administrator urged You to surrender the royal patent so he could be raised as filial and incorrupt; You said: 'What forebears granted cannot be altered.'

units.zh: 嘗詣鎮軍賈混，混以人訟事示攸，使決之。
units.en: At camp commandant Jia Hun's interview he was handed a civil suit to judge.
units.literal: Thereupon he visited General Who Garrisons the Army Jia Hun; Hun showed him a commoner's lawsuit and had him decide it.

units.zh: 攸不視，曰：「孔子稱聽訟吾猶人也，必也使無訟乎！」
units.en: You would not look at it and said: 'Confucius said, "In hearing lawsuits I am like others—surely the task is to make lawsuits cease!"'
units.literal: You would not look at it and said: 'Confucius said, "In hearing lawsuits I am like others—surely the task is to make lawsuits cease!"'

units.zh: 混奇之，以女妻焉。
units.en: Jia Hun admired him and married him to his daughter.
units.literal: Hun marveled at him and gave him his daughter as wife.

units.zh: 舉灼然二品，為吳王文學，曆太子洗馬、東海王越參軍。
units.en: Rated ‘brilliant’ second grade, he became literary instructor to the Prince of Wu, then served in succession as Foreman Clerk of the Heir Apparent (xianma) and as adjutant to Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai.
units.literal: Raised in the Zhuoran second-grade category; he became literary instructor to the Prince of Wu; served successively as prince's tutor to the heir, staff to Prince Donghai Sima Yue.

units.zh: 越欽其為人，轉為世子文學、吏部郎。
units.en: Sima Yue esteemed him and moved him to heir's tutor and personnel director.
units.literal: Yue admired his conduct and transferred him to heir's literary instructor and bureau chief in the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 越弟騰為東中郎將，請攸為長史。
units.en: Sima Teng, east-center general, took him as chief clerk.
units.literal: Yue's younger brother Teng was General of the Center East and requested You as senior clerk.

units.zh: 出為河東太守。
units.en: He governed Hedong.
units.literal: He went out as Administrator of Hedong.

units.zh: 永嘉末，沒于石勒。
units.en: Yongjia's collapse delivered him to Shi Le.
units.literal: At the end of Yongjia he fell into Shi Le's hands.

units.zh: 然勒宿忌諸官長二千石，聞攸在營，馳召，將殺之。
units.en: Shi Le despised former prefects; hearing Deng You's rank, he planned execution.
units.literal: Yet Le long nursed hatred for officials at two thousand shi; hearing You was in camp, he urgently summoned him intending to kill him.

units.zh: 攸至門，門幹乃攸為郎時幹，識攸，攸求紙筆作辭。
units.en: At the gate an old clerk recognized him and slipped him brush and paper for a plea.
units.literal: When You reached the gate, the gate guard had been You's clerk when he was a gentleman; recognizing You, You asked for brush and paper to compose a petition.

units.zh: 幹候勒和悅，致之。
units.en: The clerk waited for Shi Le's good humor and submitted it.
units.literal: The clerk waited until Le was mild of mood and presented it.

units.zh: 勒重其辭，乃勿殺。
units.en: Shi Le admired the prose and spared him.
units.literal: Le prized his wording and thereupon did not kill him.

units.zh: 勒長史張賓先與攸比舍，重攸名操，因稱攸於勒。
units.en: Chief clerk Zhang Bin, once his neighbor, praised Deng You until Shi Le listened.
units.literal: Le's senior clerk Zhang Bin had formerly lived next door to You and esteemed You's reputation and conduct; thereupon he praised You to Le.

units.zh: 勒召至幕下，與語，悅之，以為參軍，給車馬。
units.en: Summoned to HQ, Deng You won a staff post with mounts.
units.literal: Le summoned him to his tent; conversing, he was pleased and appointed him adjutant with carriage and horses.

units.zh: 勒每東西，置攸車營中。
units.en: Every campaign parked Deng You's wagon in headquarters.
units.literal: Whenever Le marched east or west he stationed You's cart in camp.

units.zh: 勒夜禁火，犯之者死。
units.en: Shi Le banned night fires on penalty of death.
units.literal: Le forbade fire by night on pain of death.

units.zh: 攸與胡鄰轂，胡夜失火燒車。
units.en: A Hu neighbor's campfire torched the wagon train.
units.literal: You camped beside a Hu neighbor; the Hu lost fire by night and burned the carts.

units.zh: 吏按問，胡乃誣攸。
units.en: Guards questioned the Hu, who blamed Deng You.
units.literal: Clerks investigated; the Hu then falsely accused You.

units.zh: 攸度不可與爭，遂對以弟婦散發溫酒為辭。
units.en: Knowing argument was useless, he claimed his sister-in-law had warmed wine by night—a face-saving fiction.
units.literal: You judged he could not contend with them and replied with the excuse that his sister-in-law had loosened her hair warming wine.

units.zh: 勒赦之。
units.en: Shi Le accepted the excuse.
units.literal: Le pardoned him.

units.zh: 既而胡人深感，自縛詣勒以明攸，而陰遺攸馬驢，諸胡莫不歎息宗敬之。
units.en: The Hu, ashamed, confessed to Shi Le and sent Deng You livestock; tribesmen revered him.
units.literal: Afterward the Hu were deeply moved; they bound themselves and went to Le to clear You, while secretly presenting horses and donkeys to You—all the Hu sighed and revered him.

units.zh: 石勒過泗水，攸乃斫壞車，以牛馬負妻子而逃。
units.en: At the Si crossing he smashed the cart and fled with family on draft animals.
units.literal: When Shi Le crossed the Si River, You broke up his cart and fled carrying wife and children on oxen and horses.

units.zh: 又遇賊，掠其牛馬，步走，擔其兒及其弟子綏。
units.en: Bandits stole the beasts; he walked, bearing his son and nephew Sui.
units.literal: Again he met bandits who stripped his oxen and horses; he went on foot, carrying his son and his nephew Sui.

units.zh: 度不能兩全，乃謂其妻曰：「吾弟早亡，唯有一息，理不可絕，止應自棄我兒耳。
units.en: Judging he could not save both, he told his wife: 'My younger brother died early and left only this breath of life—the line cannot end; I must abandon only my own son.
units.literal: Judging he could not save both, he told his wife: 'My younger brother died early and left only this breath of life—the line cannot end; I must abandon only my own son.

units.zh: 幸而得存，我後當有子。」
units.en: If we are fortunate enough to survive, I shall yet have sons.'
units.literal: If we are fortunate enough to survive, I shall yet have sons.'

units.zh: 妻泣而從之，乃棄之。
units.en: She wept and consented; they left his son behind.
units.literal: His wife wept and obeyed; thereupon they abandoned [the son].

units.zh: 其子朝棄而暮及。
units.en: The boy abandoned at dawn somehow reached them by dusk.
units.literal: The son abandoned in the morning caught up by evening.

units.zh: 明日，攸繋之於樹而去。
units.en: Next morning Deng You bound his son to a tree and walked on.
units.literal: The next day You tied him to a tree and departed.

units.zh: 至新鄭，投李矩。
units.en: They reached Li Ju at Xinzheng.
units.literal: Reaching Xinzheng he threw himself on Li Ju's protection.

units.zh: 三年，將去，而矩不聽。
units.en: Three years later Li Ju refused his request to leave.
units.literal: After three years he wished to leave but Ju would not hear of it.

units.zh: 荀組以為陳郡、汝南太守，湣帝徵為尚書左丞、長水校尉，皆不果就。
units.en: Imperial appointments from Xun Zu and Emperor Min never materialized.
units.literal: Xun Zu appointed him Administrator of Chen commandery and Runan; Emperor Min summoned him as vice director of the left of the Masters of Writing and colonel of Changshui—none of these posts came to fruition.

units.zh: 後密捨矩去，投荀組於許昌，矩深恨焉，久之，乃送家屬還攸。
units.en: He fled secretly to Xuchang; Li Ju resented it but eventually returned his household.
units.literal: Later he secretly slipped away from Ju and joined Xun Zu at Xuchang; Ju deeply resented it; after a long while he sent You's family back.

units.zh: 攸與刁協、周顗素厚，遂至江東。
units.en: He crossed to the south with Diao Xie and Zhou Yi.
units.literal: You was always close to Diao Xie and Zhou Yi; he thereupon reached the eastern Yangzi.

units.zh: 元帝以攸為太子中庶子。
units.en: Emperor Yuan named him palace aide to the heir.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him attendant of the crown prince's household.

units.zh: 時吳郡闕守，人多欲之，帝以授攸。
units.en: Everyone wanted Wu commandery; the throne gave it to Deng You.
units.literal: At that time Wu commandery lacked an administrator; many coveted it; the emperor gave it to You.

units.zh: 攸載米之郡，俸祿無所受，唯飲吳水而已。
units.en: He arrived carrying grain for relief, took no salary, and drank only local river water.
units.literal: You shipped grain to the commandery; he accepted no salary—only drank Wu's water.

units.zh: 時郡中大饑，攸表振貸，未報，乃輒開倉救之。
units.en: Famine struck; before capital approval he opened state granaries.
units.literal: At that time the commandery suffered great famine; You memorialized for relief grain; before reply came he opened the granaries and saved the people.

units.zh: 臺遣散騎常侍桓彝、虞慰勞饑人，觀聽善不，乃劾攸以擅出穀。
units.en: The court sent Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Huan Yi, together with Yu, to comfort the starving and see whether affairs stood well, then impeached You for issuing grain without authorization.
units.literal: The court sent Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Huan Yi and Yu to comfort the starving and observe whether things were well, then impeached You for unauthorized grain issue.

units.zh: 俄而有詔原之。
units.en: An edict soon absolved him.
units.literal: Shortly an edict pardoned him.

units.zh: 攸在郡刑政清明，百姓歡悅，為中興良守。
units.en: His Wu tenure brought lucid justice—acclaimed minister of the restoration.
units.literal: You in the commandery governed with clear punishments and administration; the common people rejoiced; he was a fine administrator of the restoration.

units.zh: 後稱疾去職。
units.en: Illness became his excuse to resign.
units.literal: Later he pleaded illness and left office.

units.zh: 郡常有送迎錢數百萬，攸去郡，不受一錢。
units.en: Locals offered millions in parting gifts; he refused every coin.
units.literal: The commandery routinely offered several million in send-off and welcome money; when You left the commandery he accepted not one coin.

units.zh: 百姓數千人留牽攸船，不得進，攸乃小停，夜中發去。
units.en: Thousands gripped his boat until he feigned a stop and fled by night.
units.literal: Several thousand common people held his boat and would not let it advance; You briefly halted, then slipped away by night.

units.zh: 吳人歌之曰：「紞如打五鼓，雞鳴天欲曙。
units.en: The people of Wu sang: "The drum rolls like the fifth watch; the cock crows—dawn nears.
units.literal: The people of Wu sang: "The drum rolls like the fifth watch; the cock crows—dawn nears.

units.zh: 鄧侯挽不留，謝令推不去。」
units.en: Minister Deng cannot be held back; Magistrate Xie cannot be turned away."
units.literal: Minister Deng cannot be held back; Magistrate Xie cannot be turned away."

units.zh: 百姓詣臺乞留一歲，不聽。
units.en: They petitioned the court for one more year; it refused.
units.literal: The common people went to the ministry begging he stay one year; they were not permitted.

units.zh: 拜侍中。
units.en: He became palace attendant.
units.literal: He was appointed palace attendant.

units.zh: 歲餘，轉吏部尚書。
units.en: A year later he directed personnel.
units.literal: After more than a year he was transferred Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 蔬食弊衣，周急振乏。
units.en: He lived on greens and rags while aiding the needy.
units.literal: He ate vegetables and wore worn clothes; he relieved emergencies and aided the destitute.

units.zh: 性謙和，善與人交，賓無貴賤，待之若一，而頗敬媚權貴。
units.en: Humble with guests yet currying powerful patrons.
units.literal: By nature modest and agreeable, skilled in dealing with people, he treated guests high or low alike—yet inclined to flatter the powerful.

units.zh: 永昌中，代周顗為護軍將軍，
units.en: Yongchang era: he succeeded Zhou Yi as guards general.
units.literal: In the Yongchang era he replaced Zhou Yi as General Who Guards the Army.

units.zh: 太寧二年，王敦反，明帝密謀起兵，乃遷攸為會稽太守。
units.en: In the second year of Taining, when Wang Dun rebelled, Emperor Ming secretly planned to raise troops and thereupon transferred You to Administrator of Kuaiji.
units.literal: In the second year of Taining, when Wang Dun rebelled, Ming secretly plotted to raise troops; thereupon he transferred You to Administrator of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 初，王敦伐都之後，中外兵數每月言之於敦。
units.en: After Wang Dun's coup, monthly troop returns still went to him.
units.literal: Originally, after Wang Dun attacked the capital, inner and outer troop figures were reported to Dun each month.

units.zh: 攸已出在家，不復知護軍事，有惡攸者，誣攸尚白敦兵數。
units.en: A foe claimed Deng You still fed Wang Dun troop counts.
units.literal: You had already left office and no longer knew guards affairs; someone who hated You falsely claimed You still reported troop numbers to Dun.

units.zh: 帝聞而未之信，轉攸為太常。
units.en: The emperor doubted the tale and moved him to minister of ceremonies.
units.literal: The emperor heard it but did not believe; he transferred You to Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 時帝南郊，攸病不能從。
units.en: During the suburban sacrifice Deng You was too ill to attend.
units.literal: At that time the emperor performed southern suburb rites; You was ill and could not follow.

units.zh: 車駕過攸問疾，攸力病出拜。
units.en: The imperial train stopped at his door; he dragged himself out to bow.
units.literal: The imperial carriage passed You's home to inquire after his illness; You forced himself gravely ill to go out and bow.

units.zh: 有司奏攸不堪行郊而拜道左，坐免。
units.en: Officials impeached him for bowing trackside while skipping the rite—he was stripped of office.
units.literal: The relevant offices reported You could not perform suburb rites yet bowed beside the road; he was punished by dismissal.

units.zh: 攸每有進退，無喜慍之色。
units.en: Promotion or demotion never touched his expression.
units.literal: Whenever You advanced or retreated in office he showed neither joy nor anger.

units.zh: 久之，遷尚書右僕射。
units.en: He eventually became vice president of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: After a long while he was promoted vice director of the right of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 咸和元年卒，贈光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，祠以少年。
units.en: In the first year of Xianhe he died; posthumous honors included minister of the imperial household, a gold seal and purple ribbon, and sacrifice with a young pig.
units.literal: In the first year of Xianhe, he died; posthumously awarded Minister of the Imperial Household with gold seal and purple ribbon; sacrifice with a young pig.

units.zh: 攸棄子之後，妻子不復孕。
units.en: After abandoning his son his wife bore none.
units.literal: After You abandoned his son, his wife conceived no more.

units.zh: 過江，納妾，甚寵之，訊其家屬，說是北人遭亂，憶父母姓名，乃攸之甥。
units.en: Across the river he favored a concubine who proved, under questioning, to be his niece.
units.literal: South of the Yangzi he took a concubine whom he favored; questioning her family, she said she was a northerner lost in chaos—recalling parents' names, she was You's niece.

units.zh: 攸素有德行，聞之感恨，遂不復畜妾，卒以無嗣。
units.en: Mortified, he dismissed concubines and died childless.
units.literal: You had always cultivated virtue; hearing this he was stricken with regret and kept no more concubines; he ended without heir.

units.zh: 時人義而哀之，為之語曰：「天道無知，使鄧伯道無兒。」
units.en: People of the time deemed him righteous and pitied him, saying for him: 'Heaven's way is blind—it left Deng Bodao without sons.'
units.literal: People of the time deemed him righteous and pitied him, saying for him: 'Heaven's way is blind—it left Deng Bodao without sons.'

units.zh: 弟子綏服攸喪三年。
units.en: Nephew Deng Sui mourned him three years.
units.literal: His nephew Sui observed mourning for You three years.

units.zh: 吳隱之
units.en: Wu Yin-zhi
units.literal: Wu Yin-zhi

units.zh: 吳隱之，字處默，濮陽鄄城人，魏侍中質六世孫也。
units.en: Wu Yin-zhi (courtesy Chumo), a man of Juancheng in Puyang, was a sixth-generation descendant of Wei attendant Wu Zhi.
units.literal: Wu Yin-zhi, courtesy name Chumo, was a man of Juancheng in Puyang; sixth-generation descendant of attendant of the inner court Zhi in Wei.

units.zh: 隱之美姿容，善談論，博涉文史，以儒雅標名。
units.en: Handsome, eloquent, learned—known as a Confucian gentleman.
units.literal: Yin-zhi had handsome features, excelled at discourse, read broadly in literature and history, and was famed for refined scholarship.

units.zh: 弱冠而介立，有清操，雖日晏歠菽，不饗非其粟，儋石無儲，不取非其道。
units.en: Young but austere: he starved rather than eat ill-gotten food.
units.literal: At the capping age he stood apart with pure conduct: though he supped bean gruel at sunset, he would not eat grain not his own; though he stored not a stone of grain, he would not take by paths unjust.

units.zh: 年十餘，丁父憂，每號泣，行人為之流涕。
units.en: When he was a little over ten he suffered his father's death; whenever he wailed, passersby wept.
units.literal: At over ten years he suffered his father's loss; whenever he wailed, passersby wept.

units.zh: 事母孝謹，及其執喪，哀毀過禮。
units.en: Serving his mother he was filial and careful; when he observed mourning, his grief exceeded ritual.
units.literal: Serving his mother he was filial and careful; when observing mourning his grief exceeded ritual.

units.zh: 家貧，無人鳴鼓，每至哭臨之時，恆有雙鶴警叫，及祥練之夕，復有群雁俱集，時人咸以為孝感所至。
units.en: Poor families lacked funeral drums; cranes and wild geese answered his obsequies—called heaven's echo of his grief.
units.literal: The family was poor and none could beat the drum [for rituals]; whenever they reached the weeping portion of the rites, a pair of cranes always cried aloud; on the nights of xiang and lian ceremonies flocks of geese gathered—all considered it moved by sympathetic resonance.

units.zh: 嘗食咸菹，以其味旨，掇而棄之。
units.en: Tasting savory pickles during mourning, he spat them out for excess pleasure.
units.literal: Once he ate salted pickles; finding the taste delicious, he picked out and discarded [the pieces].

units.zh: 與太常韓康伯鄰居，康伯母，殷浩之姊，賢明婦人也，每聞隱之哭聲，輟餐投箸，為之悲泣。
units.en: Han Kangbo's mother, Yin Hao's sister, wept whenever Wu Yin-zhi wailed next door.
units.literal: He neighbored Minister of Ceremonies Han Kangbo; Kangbo's mother, elder sister of Yin Hao, was a worthy woman; whenever she heard Yin-zhi's weeping she stopped eating and threw down chopsticks, weeping in sorrow.

units.zh: 既而謂康伯曰：「汝若居銓衡，當舉如此輩人。」
units.en: Afterward she told Kangbo: 'If you ever hold personnel authority, raise men like this.'
units.literal: Afterward she told Kangbo: 'If you ever hold personnel authority, raise men like this.'

units.zh: 及康伯為吏部尚書，隱之遂階清級，解褐輔國功曹，轉參征虜軍事。
units.en: When Han Kangbo took personnel, Wu Yin-zhi rose from clerk to campaign staff.
units.literal: When Kangbo became Minister of Personnel, Yin-zhi thereupon ascended to pure ranks; leaving common cloth he became clerk of merit for General Who Supports the State, then transferred as administrator on the staff of the General Who Campaigns Against the Caitiffs.

units.zh: 兄坦之為袁真功曹，真敗，將及禍，隱之詣桓溫，乞代兄命，溫矜而釋之。
units.en: He offered his life to Huan Wen to save brother Wu Tan-zhi after Yuan Zhen's fall.
units.literal: His elder brother Tan-zhi was clerk of merit to Yuan Zhen; when Zhen fell and disaster threatened, Yin-zhi went to Huan Wen begging to die in his brother's stead; Wen pitied him and released Tan-zhi.

units.zh: 遂為溫所知賞，拜奉朝請、尚書郎，累遷晉陵太守。
units.en: Huan Wen favored him; he reached Jinling prefect.
units.literal: Thereupon he was known and prized by Wen; appointed court gentleman preparatory, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; repeatedly promoted Administrator of Jinling.

units.zh: 在郡清儉，妻自負薪。
units.en: As prefect his wife gathered firewood.
units.literal: In the commandery he was pure and frugal; his wife herself carried firewood.

units.zh: 入為中書侍郎、國子博士、太子右衛率，轉散騎常侍，領著作郎。
units.en: Central posts stacked up—secretariat, academy, heir's guard, and historian.
units.literal: He entered [court] as vice director of the Secretariat, academician of the imperial academy, and commander of the heir's right guard; transferred to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, concurrently compiler.

units.zh: 孝武帝欲用為黃門郎，以隱之貌類簡文帝，乃止。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowu cancelled a yellow-gate post fearing he looked like Emperor Jianwen.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu wished to make him palace gentleman to the yellow gate but stopped because Yin-zhi resembled Emperor Jianwen in appearance.

units.zh: 尋守廷尉、秘書監、御史中丞，領著作如故，遷左衛將軍。
units.en: He headed justice, the palace library, and censors while editing histories.
units.literal: Shortly he acted as commandant of justice, director of the Palace Library, censor-in-chief—still concurrent compiler—promoted General of the Left Guard.

units.zh: 雖居清顯，祿賜皆班親族，冬月無被，嘗浣衣，乃披絮，勤苦同於貧庶。
units.en: He shared salary with relatives and slept under patched cotton like a pauper.
units.literal: Though occupying eminent purity, he gave stipends to kin; in winter he lacked quilts; he washed his clothes and wore wadding—working as hard as the poor.

units.zh: 廣州包帶山海，珍異所出，一篋之寶，可資數世，然多瘴疫，人情憚焉。
units.en: Guangzhou brimmed with pearls but also fever airs men dreaded.
units.literal: Guangzhou wraps mountains and sea; rare treasures issue forth—a chest of goods can enrich generations—yet miasma abounds and hearts shrink.

units.zh: 唯貧窶不能自立者，求補長史，故前後刺史皆多黷貨。
units.en: Broke men sought the post; predecessors lined their pockets.
units.literal: Only the destitute who could not stand on their own sought staff posts, so former inspectors mostly grew rich from bribes.

units.zh: 朝廷欲革嶺南之弊，隆安中，以隱之為龍驤將軍、廣州刺史、假節，領平越中郎將。
units.en: Long'an reforms sent Wu Yin-zhi as dragon general and Guangzhou inspector with Yue-pacification colonelcy.
units.literal: The court wished to reform Lingnan's abuses; in Long'an it appointed Yin-zhi General Who Rouses the Dragon, Inspector of Guang Province with credentials, concurrent colonel who pacifies the Yue.

units.zh: 未至州二十里，地名石門，有水曰貪泉，飲者懷無厭之欲。
units.en: Before the city, Greedy Spring at Shimen was said to inflame covetousness.
units.literal: Twenty li short of the provincial seat lies Shimen, where a spring called Greedy Water makes whoever drinks it harbor insatiable desire.

units.zh: 隱之既至，語其親人曰：「不見可欲，使心不亂。
units.en: When Yin-zhi arrived he told his kin: 'Not seeing what can be desired keeps the mind unperturbed.
units.literal: When Yin-zhi arrived he told his kin: 'Not seeing what can be desired keeps the mind unperturbed.

units.zh: 越嶺喪清，吾知之矣。」
units.en: To lose purity crossing the ranges—I understand how that happens.'
units.literal: To lose purity crossing the ranges—I understand how that happens.'

units.zh: 乃至泉所，酌而飲之，因賦詩曰：「古人云此水，一歃懷千金。
units.en: Thereupon he went to the spring, scooped and drank, and composed a poem: "Men of old spoke of this water—one sip loads the breast with desire worth a thousand in gold.
units.literal: Thereupon he went to the spring, scooped and drank, and composed a poem: "Men of old spoke of this water—one sip loads the breast with desire worth a thousand in gold.

units.zh: 試使夷齊飲，終當不易心。」
units.en: Try offering it to Bo Yi and Shu Qi—they would never change their hearts."
units.literal: Try offering it to Bo Yi and Shu Qi—they would never change their hearts."

units.zh: 及在州，清操逾厲，常食不過菜及幹魚而已，帷帳器服皆付外庫，時人頗謂其矯，然亦終始不易。
units.en: As prefect he tightened austerity—greens and dried fish, gear warehoused—critics called him theatrical but he never wavered.
units.literal: While in the province his pure conduct grew sterner; ordinarily he ate nothing beyond vegetables and dried fish; curtains, utensils, and clothing all went to the outer treasury—people thought him affected, yet from first to last he never altered.

units.zh: 帳下人進魚，每剔去骨存肉，隱之覺其用意，罰而黜焉。
units.en: When aides served deboned fish to curry favor, he cashiered them.
units.literal: Camp followers presented fish, always boning out meat; Yin-zhi perceived their intent and fined and dismissed them.

units.zh: 元興初，詔曰：「夫孝行篤於閨門，清節厲乎風霜，實立人之所難，而君子之美致也。
units.en: At the start of Yuanxing an edict said: "Filial conduct rooted in inner chambers, pure integrity tempered by frost and wind—such things are truly hard for ordinary men yet mark the finest gentlemen.
units.literal: At the start of Yuanxing an edict said: "Filial conduct rooted in inner chambers, pure integrity tempered by frost and wind—such things are truly hard for ordinary men yet mark the finest gentlemen.

units.zh: 龍驤將軍、廣州刺史吳隱之孝友過人，祿均九族，菲己潔素，儉愈魚飧。
units.en: General Who Rouses the Dragon, Inspector of Guangzhou Wu Yin-zhi surpasses others in filial devotion and friendship, divides stipends among nine branches of kin, keeps himself spare and pure, more frugal than a meal of fish alone.
units.literal: General Who Rouses the Dragon, Inspector of Guangzhou Wu Yin-zhi surpasses others in filial devotion and friendship, divides stipends among nine branches of kin, keeps himself spare and pure, more frugal than a meal of fish alone.

units.zh: 夫處可欲之地，而能不改其操，饗惟錯之富，而家人不易其服，革奢務嗇，南域改觀，朕有嘉焉。
units.en: Standing where desire could strike yet not changing his integrity; facing piled riches yet his household changes not its clothing—rejecting extravagance for thrift, he altered southern outlook—I approve.
units.literal: Standing where desire could strike yet not changing his integrity; facing piled riches yet his household changes not its clothing—rejecting extravagance for thrift, he altered southern outlook—I approve.

units.zh: 可進號前將軍，賜錢五十萬、穀千斛。」
units.en: He may advance to General of the Front; grant fifty myriad cash and one thousand hu of grain."
units.literal: He may advance to General of the Front; grant fifty myriad cash and one thousand hu of grain."

units.zh: 及盧循寇南海，隱之率厲將士，固守彌時，長子曠之戰沒。
units.en: Lu Xun struck Guangzhou; Wu Yin-zhi held the walls until his heir Wu Kuang-zhi fell.
units.literal: When Lu Xun raided Nanhai, Yin-zhi rallied officers and soldiers and held firm for a long time; his eldest son Kuang-zhi died in battle.

units.zh: 循攻擊百有餘日，逾城放火，焚燒三千餘家，死者萬餘人，城遂陷。
units.en: After a hundred-day siege Lu Xun fired the suburbs, killing tens of thousands before the city collapsed.
units.literal: Xun attacked over a hundred days, crossed the walls with fire, burned more than three thousand households—over ten thousand dead—and the city fell.

units.zh: 隱之攜家累出，欲奔還都，為循所得。
units.en: Wu Yin-zhi fled with family toward Jiankang but Lu Xun seized them.
units.literal: Yin-zhi brought his household out, wished to flee back to the capital, and was captured by Xun.

units.zh: 循表朝廷，以隱之党附桓玄，宜加裁戮，詔不許。
units.en: Lu Xun accused him of siding with Huan Xuan; the court refused execution.
units.literal: Xun memorialized the court that Yin-zhi had attached to Huan Xuan and should be executed; an edict refused.

units.zh: 劉裕與循書，令遣隱之還，久方得反。
units.en: Liu Yu wrote Xun ordering Yin-zhi returned; only after a long interval did he come back.
units.literal: Liu Yu wrote Xun ordering Yin-zhi returned; only after a long interval did he come back.

units.zh: 歸舟之日，裝無餘資。
units.en: His return junk carried no private fortune.
units.literal: On the day his boat turned homeward his baggage held no surplus wealth.

units.zh: 及至，數畝小宅，籬垣仄陋，內外茅屋六間，不容妻子。
units.en: Home was a few acres of hut—six thatched rooms too tight for his household.
units.literal: Upon arrival he had a small compound of several mu; hedges narrow and cramped; six thatched rooms inside and out—not enough space for wife and children.

units.zh: 劉裕賜車牛，更為起宅，固辭。
units.en: Liu Yu offered ox-cart and a new house; Wu Yin-zhi refused.
units.literal: Liu Yu gifted carriage and oxen and offered to build him a dwelling; he firmly declined.

units.zh: 尋拜度支尚書、太常，以竹篷為屏風，坐無氈席。
units.en: As minister of finance and rites he screened rooms with bamboo mats and sat on bare boards.
units.literal: Shortly he was appointed Minister of Revenue and Minister of Ceremonies—bamboo blinds served as screens; he sat without felt mats.

units.zh: 後遷中領軍，清儉不革，每月初得祿，裁留身糧，其餘悉分振親族，家人績紡以供朝夕。
units.en: Central guard commander pay still fed relatives after he skimmed daily rice; women spun for food.
units.literal: Later promoted central protector of the army—pure frugality unchanged; each month when stipend arrived he retained only personal grain and divided the rest among kin; the household spun and wove for daily meals.

units.zh: 時有困絕，或並日而食，身恆布衣不完，妻子不沾寸祿，
units.en: Days brought doubled hunger and patched robes—family saw none of his salary.
units.literal: Sometimes utterly destitute, sometimes eating every other day; his person always wore incomplete cloth; wife and children received none of his salary.

units.zh: 義熙八年，請老致事，優詔許之，授光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，賜錢十萬、米三百斛。
units.en: In the eighth year of Yixi, Old age retirement brought minister of the imperial household honors, purple ribbon, cash, and rice.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi, he petitioned to retire on grounds of age; a gracious edict permitted it; he was awarded Minister of the Imperial Household with gold seal and purple ribbon, granted one hundred thousand cash and three hundred hu of rice.

units.zh: 九年，卒，追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。
units.en: He died Yixi year nine with posthumous vice minister and attendant honors.
units.literal: In the ninth year he died; posthumously awarded Left Minister of the Imperial Household, with cavalier attendant-in-ordinary added.

units.zh: 隱之清操不渝，屢被褒飾，致事及於身沒，常蒙優錫顯贈，廉士以為榮。
units.en: Honors followed him from resignation through death—clean officials prized the recognition.
units.literal: Yin-zhi's pure conduct never wavered; repeatedly he received imperial praise; from retirement through death he constantly enjoyed generous gifts—men of integrity counted it glory.

units.zh: 初，隱之為奉朝請，謝石請為衛將軍主簿。
units.en: When Wu Yin-zhi was court gentleman, Xie Shi recruited him for the guards general's secretariat.
units.literal: Originally when Yin-zhi was court gentleman preparatory, Xie Shi requested him as chief clerk to General Who Guards the Army.

units.zh: 隱之將嫁女，石知其貧素，遣女必當率薄，乃令移廚帳助其經營。
units.en: Knowing the wedding would be bare, Xie Shi shipped kitchens and tents to help.
units.literal: When Yin-zhi was about to marry off his daughter, Shi knew his poverty and plainness—that a send-off must be meager—thereupon ordered kitchen and tent moved to assist preparations.

units.zh: 使者至，方見婢牽犬賣之，此外蕭然無辦。
units.en: Envoys found only a maidservant selling a dog—nothing else ready.
units.literal: When the messenger arrived he saw only a maid leading a dog to sell—beyond that nothing whatsoever had been prepared.

units.zh: 後至自番禺，其妻劉氏齎沈香一斤，隱之見之，遂投於湖亭之水。
units.en: His wife brought aloeswood from Guangzhou; he dumped it into the lake kiosk.
units.literal: Later returning from Panyu, his wife Liu carried one jin of aloeswood; Yin-zhi seeing it threw it into Lake pavilion waters.

units.zh: 子延之復厲清操，為鄱陽太守。
units.en: Son Wu Yan-zhi governed Poyang with equal austerity.
units.literal: Son Yan-zhi likewise upheld pure conduct; became Administrator of Poyang.

units.zh: 延之弟及子為郡縣者，常以廉慎為門法，雖才學不逮隱之，而孝悌潔敬猶為不替。
units.en: Younger kin in county office inherited his cautious integrity—less gifted but equally dutiful.
units.literal: Yan-zhi's younger brothers and sons who served in commanderies and counties always took integrity and caution as house rule; though talent did not match Yin-zhi's, filial piety, brotherliness, purity, and reverence did not decline.

units.zh: 【史論】
units.en: Historians' appraisal
units.literal: 【Historical Commentary】

units.zh: 史臣曰：魯芝等建旟剖竹，布政宣條，存樹威恩，沒留遺愛，咸見知明主，流譽當年。
units.en: The editors praise these prefects for governance that won both sovereigns and commoners.
units.literal: The historians say: Lu Zhi and the others unfurled command banners and wielded split bamboo tallies, spread governance and proclaimed ordinances; alive they planted awe and kindness, dead they left lingering love—all were recognized by enlightened sovereigns and enjoyed praise in their own day.

units.zh: 若伯武之潔己克勤，顏遠之申冤緩獄，鄧攸贏糧以述職，吳隱酌水以厲精，晉代良能，此焉為最。
units.en: Hu Wei, Cao Shu, Deng You, and Wu Yin-zhi epitomized Jin integrity.
units.literal: Such as Bowu's purifying himself and mastering diligence, Yuanyuan's rectifying wrongs and easing prisons, Deng You bearing grain to office, Wu Yin-zhi scooping water to steel his essence—among Jin administrators these were the ablest.

units.zh: 而攸棄子存侄，以義斷恩，若力所不能，自可割情忍痛，何至預加徽纆，絕其奔走者乎！
units.en: Yet You abandoned his son to preserve his nephew, severing affection by righteousness—if strength truly failed, one might cut feeling and endure pain—why beforehand bind him with fetters and cut off one who would run to help!
units.literal: Yet You abandoned his son to preserve his nephew, severing affection by righteousness—if strength truly failed, one might cut feeling and endure pain—why beforehand bind him with fetters and cut off one who would run to help!

units.zh: 斯豈慈父仁人之所用心也？
units.en: Would a humane father act so?
units.literal: Could this be what loving fathers and humane men intend in their hearts?

units.zh: 卒以絕嗣，宜哉！
units.en: Childlessness suited such choices.
units.literal: Ending without heirs—fitting indeed!

units.zh: 勿謂天道無知，此乃有知矣。
units.en: Heaven noticed.
units.literal: Say not Heaven's way is blind—here Heaven plainly sees.

units.zh: 世英盡節曹氏，犯門斬關，宣帝收雷霆之威，獎忠貞之烈，豈非既已在我，欲其罵人者歟！
units.en: Lu Zhi exhausted fidelity to the house of Cao, forcing gates and breaking barriers; Emperor Xuan stayed his thunderbolt wrath and rewarded that steadfast loyalty—once mastery was his, did he not still want men whose integrity even critics must acknowledge?
units.literal: Shiying exhausted fidelity to the house of Cao, forcing gates and breaking barriers; Emperor Xuan held back thunderbolt wrath and rewarded steadfast loyalty—is it not that once mastery rested with him, he desired men whose integrity even critics must acknowledge!

units.zh: 贊曰：猗歟良宰，嗣美前賢。
units.en: Encomium: noble ministers inheriting ancient virtue.
units.literal: The encomium says: Ah, worthy magistrates—carrying forward the beauty of earlier sages.

units.zh: 威同禦黠，靜若烹鮮。
units.en: They daunted knaves and ruled lightly, like frying small fish.
units.literal: Awesome alike in resisting craftiness, tranquil as cooking a small fish.

units.zh: 唯嘗吳水，但挹貪泉。
units.en: Some drank Suzhou river water; others drank Greedy Spring on purpose.
units.literal: Some tasted only Wu water; others scooped only the Greedy Spring.

units.zh: 人風既偃，俗化斯遷。
units.en: When exemplars bow, folkways follow.
units.literal: Once exemplary conduct bends the way, vulgar custom shifts in turn.
